LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Denver is coming off a lackluster win vs. the Chargers, while Seattle looks to rebound after falling to the 49ers Getty Images In the Week 6 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Denver Broncos play host to the Seattle Seahawks . The Broncos are coming off their third win in the last four games, though it required a late, game-winning drive against the decrepit division rival Los Angeles Chargers . The return of Sean Payton as play-caller didn't exactly result in an explosive or efficient offense, but the Broncos did just enough to hold off L.A. and climb back over .500. The Seahawks, meanwhile, dropped to 3-2 after falling to their own division rivals in the San Francisco 49ers . The Niners moved the ball quite well against the vaunted Seattle defense, and turnovers in their own territory haunted the Seahawks and ultimately cost them the game. Will the Seahawks bounce back, or will the Broncos capture their second consecutive victory? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Broncos vs. Seahawks live Date: Thursday, Oct. 15 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: Empower Field at Mile High (Denver) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Seahawks -2.5, O/U 40.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Seahawks have the ball Let's start here: the Seahawks cannot run the ball at all. They couldn't run the ball when rookie running back Jadarian Price was healthy earlier in the season, and they haven't been able to run the ball since he's been out. The trio of Price, Emanuel Wilson and George Holani has combined for just 447 yards on 127 carries -- an average of just 3.5 per tote. The Seahawks do not get much push up front, as their backs average a mere 0.69 yards before contact per carry, a figure that ranks fourth-worst in the NFL , according to Tru Media. Their 2.83 yards after contact per carry is more respectable, ranking 14th league-wide. The Broncos will have to be careful there. They've allowed the third-fewest rushing yards before contact per carry in the league so far (0.59), but the most rushing yards after contact (3.92), thanks to a sky-high avoided tackle rate by enemy backs (30.1%). Much of that production came from Kenneth Walker III in the season opener, but even in Weeks 2 through 5, the Broncos rank in the bottom third of the league in both yards after contact per attempt and broken tackle rate. Wilson is likely to be the primary runner once again while Price and Zach Charbonnet remain sidelined. The Broncos will have to get him on the ground on the first try, limiting the yards he can gain after contact, because the Seahawks just don't create much for him in the first place. He scarcely gets more than is blocked without breaking through tackles. In the passing game, Sam Darnold has struggled to replicate last year's results -- especially over the last two weeks. In games against the Chargers and 49ers, Darnold went just 31-of-51 for 363 yards, three touchdowns and three interceptions. After leading the league in turnovers last season, Darnold has already been picked off five times in his three full appearances this season, while his yards per attempt average is down from 8.5 to just 7.7. His completion rate is down over 3 percentage points as well. Denver's pass defense has been largely good so far this year, with the Broncos ranking fifth in opponents' EPA per dropback, according to Tru Media. The Broncos just held the Chargers to 82 net passing yards last week, which plays a huge role in that figure, but they've also allowed only one team ( Rams ) to top 218 net passing yards in any game so far. (The Chiefs didn't have to throw the ball very much in Week 1, though, because they did whatever they wanted on the ground.) The Broncos won't have Patrick Surtain II or Talanoa Hufanga here, and Riley Moss is listed as questionable -- all of which is a significant issue when you're going up against Jaxon Smith-Njigba , who leads the NFL in both receiving yards and receiving touchdowns. Jahdae Barron and Kris Abrams-Draine figure to see increased roles due to the cornerback injuries, while Devon Key will play more in the wake of Hufanga's absence. They'll all have their work cut out for them against JSN. The Seahawks really don't throw the ball to anyone else all that often. When the Broncos have the ball Denver might have gotten a win last week, but Sean Payton's return as play-caller didn't have much to do with it. The Broncos entered the game against the Chargers averaging a miserable 4.9 yards per play, then averaged a mere 3.9 per play in the win over Los Angeles. Bo Nix totaled just 123 yards on his 27 pass attempts, J.K. Dobbins ran for only 68 yards on his 18 carries, Jaylen Waddle caught just two of five balls thrown his way for just 19 yards ... nothing went well offensively. And nothing has gone right pretty much all year, with the exception of the second halves of the Broncos' wins over the Jaguars and Rams in Weeks 2 and 3. Two good halves in five weeks isn't much to write home about, even if those halves helped the Broncos steal a pair of wins and arrive at 3-2. Nix is essentially refusing to push the ball down the field so far this season. His average air yards per attempt in each of his first two years of his career was 7.3, according to Tru Media, but that figure has dropped all the way to 5.2 this year. He threw deep on 13.1% of his passes as a rookie and 11.8% of them last year, but he's done so on only 7.4% of his attempts this season. Nix also isn't running anymore. He scrambled 27.3% of the time when pressured during his rookie season and 16.1% of the time last season. That number is all the way down to 5.6% so far this year, meaning he's scrambled only four times in five games. All of this, combined with his insistence on checking down repeatedly, has made the pass offense feel neutered to date. Meanwhile, the Broncos also can't run the ball. Dobbins looks like he's running with a piano on his back, slogging his way to 3.6 yards per carry. RJ Harvey barely gets opportunities, but he hasn't done any better at only 3.7 yards per carry. Harvey is at least productive in the short passing game, but the Broncos de-emphasized that last week under Payton in favor of more Dobbins runs that went nowhere. The Seahawks have largely been their usual selves defensively through the first five weeks of the season. They've arrived at their two losses largely by virtue of their offense repeatedly turning the ball over against the Commanders (three times) and 49ers (four, including a fumble that resulted in a touchdown). Seattle has held opponents to the fewest passing yards in the league and the fewest net yards per attempt, and it has limited running games to the eighth-fewest yards per attempt as well. It's hard to see the Broncos snapping out of their funk against this unit. Sean Payton's return to calling plays may have let the Broncos come away with a win, but it did not result in their offense looking competent. They averaged just 3.9 yards per play against what had previously been a very bad Chargers defense. I cannot rightly expect the Broncos to get anything going against this hellacious Seattle defense. It's not like the Broncos are going to do what the 49ers did. Denver is also still banged up defensively and likely won't have Surtain here, which is obviously a problem against JSN. away.headline: Broncos-Seahawks report card: Once again, Denver defense bails out offense in win
away.blurb: After two long scoring drives that were a perfect blend of the pass and run, Denver’s offense was invisible in the second half. The Broncos gained two first downs, posted 30 yards, did not score and went three-and-out four times. They gained 32 yards on their last 10 drives, including penalties. It was a completely lackluster effort that wasted a defensive gem. If this is what Vance Joseph’s defense can look like without two All-Pro-caliber players in the secondary, watch out, AFC. Denver’s defense has put together multiple excellent games, but Thursday night was the unit’s watershed showing. Broncos' Jonathon Cooper removed from exempt list, available to play Week 7 On the boundary, the Broncos barely missed a beat despite Pat Surtain II being out with an ankle injury and Riley Moss barely playing because of a rib injury. Kris Abrams-Draine and Jahdae Barron kept Seahawks receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba in front of them for the most part and held Seattle’s other options in check. Seahawks returner Rashid Shaheed did have a huge kickoff return and a few nice punt returns, though. But what if you told them it would look like this: 2.9 yards per play, 3-of-14 on third down, a third-year quarterback rapidly regressing and an offense that's allergic to explosive plays. That's the conundrum in Denver right now, where the Broncos keep finding ways to win ugly. Thursday was the latest example, as Denver defeated the Seattle Seahawks 17-14 on “Thursday Night Football” at Empower Field. Here's The Denver Post's report card from Thursday night . Thursday was a reversal of the typical Broncos . Strong first half, dismal showing in the second. Bo Nix’s struggles are bordering on outright disasters at this point. He threw for just 107 yards on 17 completions — a strikingly low 6.3 yards per completion. A week after one of the worst games of his career, Nix followed it up with his fifth-lowest total. Denver’s wideouts are struggling to get open, as well. And while the run game showed flashes in the first half, it still finished with 2.6 yards per carry. J.K. Dobbins rushed for just 6 yards on six carries in the second half. The Broncos keep winning these games, but eventually their offense will need to hold up its end of the bargain. Every level of Denver’s defense played excellent football. The Broncos’ pass rush relentlessly attacked Sam Darnold from the interior and the edge. Que

home.headline: Broncos-Seahawks report card: Once again, Denver defense bails out offense in win
home.blurb: After two long scoring drives that were a perfect blend of the pass and run, Denver’s offense was invisible in the second half. The Broncos gained two first downs, posted 30 yards, did not score and went three-and-out four times. They gained 32 yards on their last 10 drives, including penalties. It was a completely lackluster effort that wasted a defensive gem. If this is what Vance Joseph’s defense can look like without two All-Pro-caliber players in the secondary, watch out, AFC. Denver’s defense has put together multiple excellent games, but Thursday night was the unit’s watershed showing. Broncos' Jonathon Cooper removed from exempt list, available to play Week 7 On the boundary, the Broncos barely missed a beat despite Pat Surtain II being out with an ankle injury and Riley Moss barely playing because of a rib injury. Kris Abrams-Draine and Jahdae Barron kept Seahawks receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba in front of them for the most part and held Seattle’s other options in check. Seahawks returner Rashid Shaheed did have a huge kickoff return and a few nice punt returns, though. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Everything you need to know to catch a key AFC South game in London Getty Images The Houston Texans and Jacksonville Jaguars are across the pond this week. The Jags have back-to-back international games, both taking place in London. They defeated the Philadelphia Eagles at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium last week. The last-second win put them at 4-1 on the season, tied for the second-best record in the AFC. The Texans come in with a bit different standing, sitting at 1-4, though, like the Jags, they are also coming off a win. Houston got their first win against the Tennessee Titans , who now sit at 0-5. Texans vs. Jaguars need to know Jaguars London history: The Jags are pretty much London's home team, playing there at least once a year since 2013, with the exception of 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic, with an 8-7 record across the pond. Their first-ever game in England was in 2013, a loss to the 49ers at Wembley Stadium. Their first international win was their third of the kind, a 2015 game against the Bills . And of course, their most recent win came in Week 5 against the Eagles. Marvin Harrison Jr. : The biggest news out of Houston is the addition of former No. 4 overall pick Marvin Harrison Jr. joining the team. The Jaguars have a long season to go after their first brush with the Houston Texans on Sunday, but that doesn't take away the importance of a rivalry AFC South game that could heavily impact where each team goes from here. As Jaguars head coach Liam Coen noted this week, divisional games offer a chance for a different slate of circumstances compared to typical weeks. "Know that every time that you line up against this team, it's going to be a fight. It's going to be a brawl. That's what's great about football, that's what's great about rivalries, is that you have a level of respect for each other," Coen said. "Because you know any given Sunday, anything can happen, especially in rivalry-type games and understanding what you can learn from each of these opportunities that you play against one another in, and how well you start to get to know each other in ways in terms of what they want to do, what we want to do. And that's the cat and mouse game; that's the game within the game that you have to play.” So with the Jaguars and Texans seemingly so evenly matched entering Week 6, how does the national media see this game playing out? We break it down below. National Media Picks Sports Illustrated Albert Breer: Texans Eva Geitheim: Jaguars Mitch Goldich: Jaguars Mike Kadlick: Jaguars Gilbert Manzano: Jaguars Conor Orr: Texans John Pluym: Jaguars Matt Verderame: Jaguars Pamela Maldonado: Texans Eric Moody: Jaguars Seth Walder: Texans Jeremy Bergman: Texans Brooke Cersosimo: Jaguars Gennaro Filice: Texans Bobby Kownack: Jaguars Dan Parr: Jaguars Zach Berman: Texans Jon Greenberg: Texans Larry Holder: Jaguars Chad Graff: Texans Josh Kendall: Jaguars Austin Mock: Jaguars Steven Louis Goldstein: Jaguars Jacksonville Jaguars On SI Analysis Jaguars get the nod over Houston 14-9, making this their second-tightest voting split this year after their Week 2 game against the Denver Broncos. This is not exactly surprising considering the Jaguars and Texans played each other so tightly two years ago, and considering the fact that so many had picked the Texans to win the AFC South to begin with. Houston just needed one win against the hapless Titans to draw closer to the Jaguars in terms of votes. I think this will be a close game because, on paper, these two teams are close in nearly every area. The Jaguars have a much better running game than the Texans do, but both teams have talented quarterbacks who are playing well, proven head coaches, explosive pass-catchers, strong defenses, so on and so forth. Even the biggest question for each team is the same (the offensive lines). While the Texans are 1-4, everything indicates this is a closer matchup on paper than one would think just looking at the records. With that said, I think the fact the Jaguars have been a more complete team this season is no accident and is not owrth simply tossing aside. The Jaguars have been one of the best teams in the NFL this season, and the Jaguars have more things to hang their hat on right now than this Texans squad does. I have the Jaguars 27, Texans 24 in what should be another one-score game that gets decided with a late score or stop. Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans confirmed earlier this week that Harrison Jr. would be making the trip overseas for this week's matchup, and would be due to play a certain number of snaps. But how Harrison Jr.'s first game against the Jaguars could fare has the chance to go a few different directions. After all, it's a very quick turnaround for any player to make when being traded and dropped onto a new team in a week's span, and could lead to his performance in Week 6 being a bit more limited compared to how things might look a little later into the season. So how might Harrison Jr.'s stat line look by the end of Week 6's matchup over the pond? Let's simply predict how the Texans' newest receiver could do in his official debut, and break down just how limited he could be in the offensive game plan. Predicted Stat Line: 30% snap share, 4 TAR, 3 REC, 43 YDS, 1 TD DeMeco Ryans emphasized earlier this week that Harrison Jr. would be involved in the Texans' offense as soon as this weekend. However, he also made sure to note that he won't be expected to play a super high number of snaps . "Don't expect him to come out and play all 60 snaps in the game," Ryans said on Wednesday. "But we'll make sure he gets what he needs, and make sure he's confident in what we're asking him to do." So just how many snaps could Harrison Jr. play? One outcome that could make sense is simply putting him in the role that now-former Texans wideout Jared Wayne had been in for the first few weeks. Jared Wayne and Marvin Harrison Jr. are vastly different talents, let's be clear. However, they are similarly big-bodied, outside receivers who can line up as a Z in several plays and situations, pairing pretty nicely next to the existing talent Houston has around the field at the position. Mandatory Credit: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Last week, Wayne saw a little over 30% of the snaps on offense. He went without any offensive stats being recorded throughout, but he did see as high as seven targets back in Week 2 against the Cincinnati Bengals . Last week, Wayne saw a little over 30% of the snaps on offense. He went without any offensive stats being recorded throughout, but he did see as high as seven targets back in Week 2 against the Cincinnati Bengals . Imagine Harrison Jr. simply slotting into those same snaps; likely with a bit more involvement in terms of being targeted or being a first read, but maybe not on the field for an excessive amount until he's able to get a few more weeks of practice and overall reps under his belt. A 30% snap share would likely be around the 15 to 20-snap mark. But in those limited looks, it feels likely that the Texans will involve him on a fair share of those plays––in this case, perhaps for four targets––to build up his confidence and rediscover some chemistry with his college quarterback, C.J. Stroud . And in a best-case scenario for the Texans, maybe Harrison Jr. is able to haul in his second touchdown of the season so far. If Houston is within striking distance for a score, and there's an ideal situation for Harrison Jr. to fill into, why not start off the tenure with his new team on a good note? So in all, a 3-43-1 stat line feels like a modest projection for Harrison Jr. in game one. It'd be a nice start for what hopes to be a long tenure in Houston, wouldn't overwhelm him with a ton of involvement, while also being paired with a ton of room to grow moving forward. away.blurb: Matiscik's inclusion wasn't particularly surprising, given that he also left the Eagles game with a shoulder injury. Heck, the team already signed long snapper Jacob Bobenmoyer to fill in for him. That said, Brown has been dealing with a hamstring injury for a few games and could be at risk of sitting out his second contest of the season. Montaric Brown and Ross Matisck did not practice for the Jaguars Aside from Ross Matiscik and Montaric Browns, the Jaguars listed other players on their Injury Report: Safety Eric Murray (concussion), right tackle Cole Van Lanen (knee), left guard Emmanuel Pregnon (toe), cornerback Jourdan Lewis (hamstring), cornerback Jaylon Jones (hamstring), cornerback Jarrian Jones (elbow), and rookie tight end Nate Boerkircher (back) were limited in practice Wednesday. Some of these players may have been limited participants because the team wants them to be ready Sunday. That said, all of them will be worth monitoring. Murray, in particular, has been dealing with a concussion and has yet to clear protocol. If he isn't good to go against the Texans, Keavon Merriweather and Rayuan Lane III will see an uptick in playing time for the second week in a row. On the other hand, Boerkircher has carved out a niche as a blocker . If he weren't available, Quintin Morris and Tanner Koziol will see an uptick in playing time. Montaric Brown sat out the win over the Cincinnati Bengals. He played against Philadelphia but only logged six snaps. There were no reports that Brown got injured again, so it's possible that they just wanted him to rest Wednesday. But if he misses the Texans game, Jarrian Jones, Travis Hunter, and Jourdan Lewis will be the team's top cornerbacks. The Jacksonville Jaguars placed left tackle Anton Harrison on the Injured Reserve list just a few days after he sustained a knee injury in the 19-17 win over the Philadelphia Eagles. With Harrison expected to miss at least four weeks, Walker Little is the next man up. But aside from Harrison, the Jags could be a handful of players when they play the Houston Texans in their second London game. Jacksonville dropped the initial injury report for Week 6. Cornerback Montaric Brown (hamstring) and long snapper Ross Matiscik (shoulder) were listed as non-participants. Van Lanen and Pregnon could be the biggest concerns of the bunch, though. If they aren't good to go, Waytt Milum and Daniel Faalele could step into their respective spots. That wouldn't be ideal when you take into account that the Jags are already without Anton Harrison. Cam Little then converted a 57-yard field goal as time expired to win the game for the Jags. Jacksonville has now won three straight. They lead the AFC South by two games over the Colts and three games over the Texans. away.headline: Report: Bears QB Caleb Williams to start vs. Falcons
away.blurb: Oct 17 (Field Level Media) - Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams is expected to return to the starting lineup Sunday against the Falcons in Atlanta after missing the previous three games with a hamstring injury, ESPN and NFL Network reported Saturday. The Bears officially listed Williams as questionable Friday, but he handled first-team work and continued to progress through the final two practices of the week, according to the reports. His return sets up the first NFL meeting between Williams and Atlanta quarterback Michael Penix Jr., two of the six quarterbacks selected in the first round of the 2024 NFL Draft. Chicago took Williams first overall, while the Falcons selected Penix at No. 8. Williams, who has been sidelined since injuring his right hamstring against the Minnesota Vikings on Sept. 20, practiced fully throughout the week without a setback. Coach Ben Johnson said Friday that Williams was "on track" after the quarterback increased his workload. Chicago went 2-1 without Williams. Case Keenum started a Week 3 victory over the Philadelphia Eagles before Tyson Bagent led the Bears past the New York Jets in Week 4 and started last week's loss to the Green Bay Packers. Williams has completed 36 of 55 passes for 407 yards, two touchdowns and one interception in two games this season. He also has rushed for 107 yards and two scores. The injury ended a run of 36 consecutive regular-season starts for Williams dating to the beginning of his NFL career. Penix also dealt with an injury this week after hurting his ribs in Atlanta's Week 5 loss to Baltimore. The Bears (3-2) will try to rebound from their loss at Green Bay against the Falcons (2-3).

Quarterback Caleb Williams practiced in full for a third straight day, an indication that he's poised to return to the lineup in Week 6. But Williams, who's missed the last three games, is questionable. There are some last step hurdles for him to clear, but all indications are he will be under center vs. the Falcons. Elsewhere, cornerback Kyler Gordon was also a full participant in practice all week, and he's questionable for Sunday's game as he looks to return from the PUP list. The Bears have also ruled out four players: linebacker T.J. Edwards (hamstring), running back Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe), defensive end Dayo Odeyingbo (quad) and linebacker Keyshaun Elliott (quad). The Chicago Bears are gearing up for their Week 6 game against the Atlanta Falcons, where Chicago is looking to get back on track after a brutal Week 5 loss to the Green Bay Packers . away.headline: Caleb Williams Injury Update, Latest on QB's Status for Bears-Falcons, Severity of Hamstring Tear
away.blurb: "Before you start asking, (I) do not know if I'm playing yet," the Chicago Bears quarterback told reporters Thursday while revealing he still must undergo stress testing and pass medical protocols before he will be cleared to return. And while he seems to be ready to return, Williams said he wasn't happy with the reporting and reaction to his setback he called a "hamstring tear" that was "pretty serious." He was listed as a full participant in practice for the second consecutive day on Thursday, suggesting he is nearing a return. What's more, he also changed his Instagram profile picture to a photo of John Wick with a bio that read, "I'm inevitable." "He's doing a great job progressing and we'll see when we can make him available to help us win ball games," head coach Ben Johnson told reporters Monday. "But he's itching to get back as soon as he can, which is a good thing, and when we get the green light, we'll move forward from there." Caleb Williams is expected to start against the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport. Williams previously said that he doesn't know if he would be on the field for Sunday's game. Williams suffered a hamstring injury during Chicago's Week 2 loss to the Minnesota Vikings. When he was carted off the field, Bears fans likely feared he would be lost for the season. Williams' status has been the biggest ongoing storyline surrounding the Bears. Johnson also said he believed the Bears "have three guys that can win games in this league." Chicago has done more than just tread water during Williams' absence, as Case Keenum led it to a 27-7 victory over the Philadelphia Eagles before Tyson Bagent directed a 23-12 win over the New York Jets. However, things took a turn last Sunday in a 31-7 blowout loss to the rival Green Bay Packers. Bagent started the game but played so poorly at 12-of-21 for 87 yards, zero touchdowns and two interceptions that Johnson put Keenum into the game to finish. It was a reminder the Bears likely need Williams healthy and under center quickly if they are going to have any realistic chance of repeating as NFC North champions. Now, it appears Williams will be back on the field this week.

home.headline: Report: Bears QB Caleb Williams to start vs. Falcons
home.blurb: Oct 17 (Field Level Media) - Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams is expected to return to the starting lineup Sunday against the Falcons in Atlanta after missing the previous three games with a hamstring injury, ESPN and NFL Network reported Saturday. The Bears officially listed Williams as questionable Friday, but he handled first-team work and continued to progress through the final two practices of the week, according to the reports. His return sets up the first NFL meeting between Williams and Atlanta quarterback Michael Penix Jr., two of the six quarterbacks selected in the first round of the 2024 NFL Draft. Chicago took Williams first overall, while the Falcons selected Penix at No. 8. Williams, who has been sidelined since injuring his right hamstring against the Minnesota Vikings on Sept. 20, practiced fully throughout the week without a setback. Coach Ben Johnson said Friday that Williams was "on track" after the quarterback increased his workload. Chicago went 2-1 without Williams. Case Keenum started a Week 3 victory over the Philadelphia Eagles before Tyson Bagent led the Bears past the New York Jets in Week 4 and started last week's loss to the Green Bay Packers. Williams has completed 36 of 55 passes for 407 yards, two touchdowns and one interception in two games this season. He also has rushed for 107 yards and two scores. The injury ended a run of 36 consecutive regular-season starts for Williams dating to the beginning of his NFL career. Penix also dealt with an injury this week after hurting his ribs in Atlanta's Week 5 loss to Baltimore. The Bears (3-2) will try to rebound from their loss at Green Bay against the Falcons (2-3).

LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict Week 6's top games Getty Images We are already in Week 6 of the NFL regular season! Can you believe it? This weekend, two AFC South rivals in the Houston Texans and Jacksonville Jaguars will battle in London, while Caleb Williams looks to return to the lineup against the Atlanta Falcons after missing the last three games. We also have an intriguing matchup in the NFC on Sunday night between the Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers , while the Washington Commanders will look to get back on track against the 49ers in San Francisco following their embarrassing tie with the New York Giants . Dan Quinn needs to find a way to get his team to refocus after they completely forgot about the clock in overtime. Which teams should you pick in Week 6, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 13 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Houston Texans vs. Jacksonville Jaguars (-3) (London) Dajani (Texans +3): The Jaguars have established themselves as one of the best teams in the AFC. While that's objectively true, they certainly aren't perfect. They probably should have dominated a short-handed Philadelphia Eagles team last week, yet didn't. Additionally, there are some questions about the offensive operation. Jacksonville went 0-3 in the red zone last week, including two trips where the Jags failed to score any points from the one-yard line. As for the Texans, they are coming off their first win of the season against the lowly Tennessee Titans . I predict they keep that momentum going and score an upset victory across the pond. DeMeco Ryans is calling defensive plays again, and C.J. Stroud is actually playing good football. He's tied for the most 20-yard completions (21) in the NFL this season. Houston is also 14-2 SU and 11-4-1 ATS in its last 16 divisional games away from home. … Prediction: Texans 21, Jaguars 18 Dubin (Jaguars -3): I think it's a real advantage that the Jaguars have already been in London for a week while the Texans haven't yet traveled across the pond. Jacksonville, as Dajani mentioned, has established itself as one of the best teams in the AFC. The offense has been efficient and explosive, and the defense has looked good as well. I know the Jags struggled with the Eagles for a bit of last week's game and probably should have lost, but Houston has only beaten a Tennessee team that is barely functional. It's not like the Texans have looked good at any point. Their defense has disappointed, and they can't run the ball whatsoever. … Prediction: Jaguars 24, Texans 20 Chicago Bears (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Falcons +3): It looks like Caleb Williams is going to return to the lineup after missing three games with his hamstring injury, and it also looks like Michael Penix Jr . will play after missing the very end of "Sunday Night Football" with his rib injury. The Chicago Bears have racked up their most rushing yards per contest (173.2) through five games since 1988, but keep an eye on the status of Kyle Monangai , who missed Week 5 with a toe injury. Last week's loss to the Packers was concerning from a defensive standpoint. The Bears have actually allowed 30 points over three straight road games (dating back to last year), which is tied for the longest streak in TEAM HISTORY. I'm going to take the points with the home team, and take Bijan Robinson and Co. to bounce back. … Prediction: Falcons 30, Bears 27 Dubin (Bears -3): The impending return of Caleb Williams has me leaning toward Chicago here. In the one non-monsoon game that Williams played, the Bears dropped 59 points on the Panthers . They ran the ball at will and created explosive plays in the passing game. Their defense was exposed a bit by the Packers last week, and the Falcons could get going offensively here ... if Michael Penix Jr. actually plays through the rib injury he suffered last week. At least some of this pick is thinking Tua Tagovailoa could start under center for Atlanta. … Prediction: Bears 23, Falcons 17 Baltimore Ravens (-4.5) at Cleveland Browns Dajani ( Ravens -4.5): I'm not going to bash the Cleveland Browns for their loss to the New York Jets in that gross weather, where punter Corey Bojorquez missed a snap and granted the Jets 34 yards of field position to set up the game-winning touchdown. But I am nervous about Cleveland's injuries with guys like Carson Schwesinger , Mason Graham , Mike Hall Jr., Tytus Howard , Quinshon Judkins and KC Concepcion banged up. I think it's fair to say that Lamar Jackson is expected back this week after sitting one game with his ankle injury, but I was wildly impressed with this Ravens defense and their ability to shut down what was statistically the hottest offense in the NFL since Michael Penix Jr. returned. Bijan Robinson rushed for 86 yards on Sunday night. He was averaging about 170 rushing yards per game with Penix under center. If it weren't for all the walking wounded in Cleveland, I would probably side with the home dogs. Not this time. … Prediction: Ravens 26, Browns 20 Dubin (Ravens -4.5): I can't tell if this line is assuming the return of Lamar Jackson or not, but r ecent reporting suggests he has a chance to return to action . If he does, I think the Ravens win this game by a lot. The Browns might be 3-2, but they have not played like an above .500 team so far. Each of their wins required a game-winning drive late in the fourth quarter, and that's not at all sustainable. I don't trust that their offense can get anything going given the various injuries to the skill-position players, and if Jackson is back, I don't think the Ravens' offense can be stopped. … Prediction: Ravens 31, Browns 14 Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles (-1.5) Dajani (Panthers +1.5): CBS Sports legend John Breech pointed out that the Eagles are facing a scheduling disadvantage this week that no team has ever been able to overcome. Philly is, of course, coming off an international game and facing a team that is coming off its bye. This has only happened four times, but the team coming off the international game is 0-4 SU and 0-3-1 ATS. That's pretty fascinating. The Eagles have covered the spread just once all season, while the last time the Panthers were on the field, they registered an impressive victory against the Detroit Lions . Bryce Young threw for 329 yards and two touchdowns, Chuba Hubbard rushed for 122 yards and two touchdowns and Tet McMillan caught 14 passes for 192 yards and -- you guessed it -- two touchdowns. I have some legitimate concerns about the Panthers defense, but I'll take the upset in Philly. … Prediction: Panthers 23, Eagles 21 Dubin (Eagles -1.5): I don't feel good about this one at all. I'm basically just throwing my hands in the air and saying, well, the Eagles can't lose again , can they? … Prediction: Eagles 20, Panthers 17 Dallas Cowboys at Green Bay Packers (-1.5) (SNF) Dajani (Packers -1.5): I told you the Packers were going to upset the Bears last week, and that something "weird" was going to happen. The "weird" came in the form of a 31-7 beatdown of Tyson Bagent . It's tough to trust Dallas after watching an undrafted rookie quarterback making his second career start come into AT&T Stadium and drop 419 yards of total offense on the Cowboys' head in prime time. Now, they have to go to Lambeau Field and try to stop a quarterback in Jordan Love , who is clearly finding his rhythm, having just thrown for 367 yards and two touchdowns. CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens are definitely a fun duo, but so are Christian Watson and Matthew Golden . Heck, let's make it a trio with tight end Tucker Kraft . … Prediction: Packers 27, Cowboys 24 Dubin (Packers -1.5): The Dallas defense is just too bad for me to feel comfortable picking the Cowboys against a team that has an offensive pulse. The Packers showed last week that they are capable of throwing the ball all over the yard even if their running game can't get going. Even with the return of Joey Porter Jr. , I expect that Green Bay will get one or all of Christian Watson, Matthew Golden and Tucker Kraft going down the field. Dallas should put up points, too, because the Packers' defense is no great shakes, but I'm taking Green Bay to win here. … Prediction: Packers 33, Cowboys 28 Washington Commanders at San Francisco 49ers (-7.5) (MNF) Dajani (49ers -7.5): I am genuinely curious how the Commanders running the clock out on themselves affected the locker room. That's something that seems hard to bounce back from, because everyone looks dumb. Obviously, the buck stops with the head coach, but why did offensive coordinator David Blough call a play that USED MOTION as precious seconds ticked off the clock, and how was quarterback Jayd

Minter said that Lamar Jackson remains “day to day” and when he’s ready, he’ll be out at practice. away.headline: Injuries cloud Browns-Ravens showdown for AFC North lead in Cleveland
away.blurb: Browns beat reporter Mary Kay Cabot laid out the scope of the problem plainly. “The Ravens have 21 on their injury report today on Thursday, and the Browns have 17,” she said. “The Ravens had two more added today, including Zay Flowers, who was limited with a toe injury. We still don’t even know if Lamar Jackson is playing in this game and we certainly know that there are plenty of Browns that are still idle, still ailing and not sure they’re going to play.” Still, there’s reason to think at least some of those names could return by Sunday. Schwesinger finished last week’s Jets game. Labbe noted that Schwesinger and Graham are “two guys that wouldn’t shock me if we walked out there (Friday) morning and they’re both in the stretch lines getting ready to go.” CLEVELAND, Ohio — 38 players. Two injury reports. Zero certainty about who will actually suit up Sunday when the Browns host the Ravens at Huntington Bank Field with first place in the AFC North on the line. That’s the impossible situation both teams — and anyone trying to analyze this game — find themselves in heading into one of the biggest divisional matchups of the young NFL season. The Browns’ injury list includes defensive cornerstones Carson Schwesinger, Mason Graham and Mike Hall — none of whom had practiced through Thursday. For a defense that’s been Cleveland’s identity all season, those aren’t small absences. Browns beat reporter Ashley Bastock zeroed in on what the late-week practice absences actually mean in practical terms. “It’s always a little concerning when you get to Thursday and they haven’t been on the practice field at all because that does become a really tight turnaround,” she said. “And I think ultimately it’s why we’re going into picking this game, really just having no clue what to do or what’s going to decide it, because it’s really hard to know those things when you don’t know who’s actually going to be on the field.” The Browns have shown real depth this season. Backup defenders Adin Huntington and Sam Kamara performed well against the Jets even without a full complement of starters. But there’s a ceiling to how much depth can compensate. As Labbe put it: “Your starters and your stars are starters and stars for a reason. And eventually, if you don’t have those guys, that can catch up to you.” The Ravens face their own uncertainty — a reshuffled offensive line, Flowers’ toe injury and a quarterback who hasn’t practiced all week. Friday’s practice will be the key for both rosters. Whatever happens, Sunday’s game may ultimately be decided less by scheme than by which injury report clears up first. ©2026 Advance Local Media LLC. Visit cleveland.com. away.blurb: Ravens Final Week 6 Injury Report: Four Players Ruled Out - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Ravens Final Week 6 Injury Report: Four Players Ruled Out While it had been established that the Ravens would likely be without quarterback Lamar Jackson for another game, he has officially been ruled out, along with three others. Center Cam Jurgens also remains out as he works his way back from concussion protocol. The Ravens traded for the former Philadelphia Eagles center before Week 5, but he was in the protocol when the trade took place. With Jurgens out, this means rookie guard Vega Ioane will step in as the center yet again. Additionally, guard Andrew Vorhees is questionable with a foot injury, and he may need more time to heal as well. Emery Jones Jr. may get the start on Sunday, especially so as not to lead to a further injury for Vorhees. The issue is that Jones is also questionable, pointing to what could be an issue if both are not able to play. Finally, defensive tackle Broderick Washington is out due to an ankle injury that he sustained in Week 5. Despite a full week of practice as a full participant, rookie receiver Ja'Kobi Lane is also questionable. He may not be ready to play, as he is still being designated to return from IR. No other players have injury statuses for the game. Despite the laundry list of injuries reported, the Ravens will have most of their key players available. Two concerns arose on Thursday when wide receiver Zay Flowers appeared on the injury report with a toe ailment, and linebacker Mike Green joined him with a hamstring. Both were limited and were upgraded to full participants on Friday. Outside linebacker Trey Hendrickson is also making his return after undergoing a procedure to fix his broken finger. The Indianapolis Colts return home to host the Tennessee Titans on Sunday, Oct. 18, with Indy favored by nearly a touchdown despite some concerning underlying metrics. My Titans vs. Colts prediction sees value in Tennessee in this AFC South showdown, with the Titans' defense giving them a legitimate chance to make things uncomfortable at Lucas Oil Stadium. Check out more NFL picks ahead of this divisional clash, with kickoff set for 1 p.m. ET on FOX. TOP Pick Titans vs Colts prediction: Titans +6.5 It's ugly, but I'd trade the Tennessee Titans +6.5, down to +5.5 , against the Indianapolis Colts . This is more of an anti-Indianapolis pick than pro-Tennessee. The Colts are 31st in net yards per play, 29th in early-down EPA per play differential, and 32nd in net quarterback pressure rate. I know the Titans suck, but should any team with that type of profile be a 6.5-point favorite? Also, after starting out last season hot, his first in Indianapolis, QB Daniel Jones is back to being terrible . Jones is 24th in adjusted EPA per play, according to RBSDM.com , and 26th in QBR. The bottom line: Jones and the Colts aren't good enough to be laying this many points . Titans vs Colts combo A Tennessee cover should correlate with an ugly, lower-scoring game, so I'm pairing Titans +6.5 with Under 44.5 and RB Tony Pollard 60+ rushing yards. Tennessee needs to shorten this game and keep QB Cam Ward out of obvious passing situations. That means establishing the run with Pollard against an Indianapolis defense ranked 27th in yards per rush allowed . That ground-heavy approach helps the Under. Neither offense has been trustworthy on late downs, and Tennessee and Indianapolis are tied for 24th in third-down conversion rate. A competitive game featuring long possessions, field goals, and limited explosive passing plays is exactly what I'm looking for. Tony Pollard Over 59.5 rushing yards Titans vs Colts touchdown scorer: Carnell Tate I'd trade Carnell Tate 's anytime touchdown probability up to 30%. Tate, the first receiver selected in the 2026 NFL Draft at No. 4 overall, is overdue for his first score. He has 37 targets this season, and Atlanta's Drake London is the only other pass-catcher with at least 37 targets who still doesn't have a receiving touchdown. The matchup also helps. All five Indianapolis starting defensive backs have failing PFF grades , while the Colts rank 22nd in defensive dropback EPA per play, according to RBSDM.com. If there's ever a spot for Tate to finally break through, this is it. Brown coming off IR ALCS Game 4 postponed Defense will win WNBA Finals NFL experts predict winner of Colts vs. Titans Week 6 game Paul Bretl, Colts Wire Fri, October 16, 2026 at 3:19 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Indianapolis Colts return home in Week 6 for a divisional matchup with the Tennessee Titans . Following last week's disappointing loss in Pittsburgh, the Colts dropped to 2-3 on the season and are in need of a win against the 0-5 Titans. But will they get it? Here is who the experts are picking to win this game. ESPN's three experts are all taking the Colts to win this game while doing so rather comfortably. ESPN's FPI prediction model also gives Indianapolis a 72.1% chance of winning this game by an average of 6.1 points. Pro Football Talk Mike Florio is picking the Colts to win 27-10. "The Colts can't afford to lose at home to a team that can't do much on either side of the ball." Pete Prisco also likes the Colts to win by multiple scores. 28-17 Indianapolis. "The winless Titans head out on the road to play a Colts team that has been inconsistent. The Colts' defense has improved in recent weeks, which will challenge Cam Ward and the Titans' limited offense. Look for the Colts to get a division victory as Jonathan Taylor has a big game." Almost a clean sweep. Four of the five NFL.com experts are picking the Colts to win. But Gennaro Filice likes the Titans -- here's why: "Admittedly, Tennessee has played like the most beatable team in the entire league, particularly on offense, where the Titans rank dead last in points and yards by comfortable margins. But Saleh's D at least has some bite, especially up front. Jeffery Simmons is an absolute force of nature, and while John Franklin-Myers has yet to validate his $63 million deal as a pass rusher, he remains quite effective against the run. Is it that hard to imagine the Titans containing Jonathan Taylor , getting just enough offense from Cam Ward and eking out a low-wattage win?" away.headline: Colts' Week 6 injury report gives fans every reason to expect a Titans win
away.blurb: The Indianapolis Colts must feel pretty good about their health because they released Darius Slayton even though the team has struggled with wide receiver injuries this season. Not so much in Week 6, even though Ashton Dulin (hamstring) is going to be out and Alec Pierce still is . The positive is that Indy has a bye week, also known as having a matchup against the Tennessee Titans. As for Alec Pierce, no timeline exists for when he might return after reinjuring his heel. That might not happen until midseason, and the Colts will probably have far tougher games than the Titans before Pierce comes back. Besides Dulin, the only Indy player who will miss the game, according to head coach Shane Steichen , is linebacker Jaylon Carlies (ribs), but both Carlies and Dulin missed Week 5, and the reason the team lost to the Pittsburgh Steelers had nothing to do with the absences of Dulin and Carlies. The reason was that the defense was terrible again. Therein lies the difference between the Steelers and the Titans, as no matter how bad Indy's defense can be at times, Tennessee doesn't have the offensive talent that Pittsburgh has. Indianapolis Colts should be healthy enough to easily defeat the Tennessee Titans in Week 6 The Titans are 31st in the NFL in yards per play (4.5), last in points scored (58), 28th in quarterback rating (77.2), and 27th in rushing yards per game (82.6). Unless Indianapolis was without defensive lineman DeForest Buckner, cornerbacks Sauce Gardner and Charvarius Ward, and most other good starters, Indianapolis should be able to outscore Tennessee easily. And Buckner, Ward, and Gardner are healthy and will play in Week 6. The Titans haven't beaten Indianapolis since October 2022, a stretch of six straight wins for the Colts, and Indy has no excuse for not making that seven straight victories at Lucas Oil Stadium on Sunday. Injuries won't be a problem for the Colts, at least heading into the game. Tennessee won't have starting safety Kevin Winston Jr., but otherwise they are mostly healthy. They just don't have a lot of talent. They haven't defeated any AFC South team since January 2024, and if that changes against the Colts in Week 6, Indianapolis needs to make some immediate changes. Ultimately, Sunday should be a get-healthy game for the Indianapolis Colts as far as record and standing in the division. When all else is going on, at least Indianapolis can count on two wins every season against the dismal Tennessee Titans . Shane Steichen on Friday ruled out linebacker Jaylon Carlies (ribs) and wide receiver Ashton Dulin (hamstring) for Sunday's game against the Tennessee Titans. Both players also missed Week 5 against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Tight ends Will Mallory (thumb) and Tyler Warren (groin) are both listed as questionable. Mallory was a full participant in practice all week, while Warren was a limited participant Friday. On the other hand, the Titans ruled out defensive tackle Jordan Elliott (personal matter) and safety Kevin Winston (quadricep). home.headline: Colts sign TE Pharaoh Brown to 53-man roster from practice squad, sign LB Germaine Pratt to practice squad
home.blurb: Colts sign TE Pharaoh Brown to 53-man roster from practice squad, sign LB Germaine Pratt to practice squad Skip to main content Primary nav SCHEDULE The Colts made the roster move on Tuesday. The Indianapolis Colts today signed tight end Pharaoh Brown to the 53-man roster from the practice squad. The team also signed linebacker Germaine Pratt to the practice squad. Brown , 6-5, 246 pounds, has spent the entire season on the team's practice squad. He has played in 94 career games (56 starts) in his time with the Colts (2026, 2023), Arizona Cardinals (2025), Miami Dolphins (2025), Seattle Seahawks (2024), New England Patriots (2023), Cleveland Browns (2018-20, 2022), Houston Texans (2020-22) and Oakland Raiders (2017-18). Brown has compiled 74 receptions for 752 yards (10.2 avg.) and three touchdowns. Pratt , 6-3, 250 pounds, re-joins Indianapolis after spending time with the team last season. He has started 104-of-112 career games in his time with the Colts (2025), Las Vegas Raiders (2025) and Cincinnati Bengals (2019-24) and has totaled 734 tackles (416 solo), 38.0 tackles for loss, 3.5 sacks, 33 passes defensed, eight interceptions, eight forced fumbles, seven fumble recoveries and eight special teams stops. Pratt has started seven postseason contests and has compiled 49 tackles (32 solo), 1.0 tackle for loss, four passes defensed and one interception. In 2025, he started 12 games with Indianapolis and registered 101 tackles (57 solo), 5.0 tackles for loss, eight passes defensed, one interception, one forced fumble and two fumble recoveries. Pratt began last season with the Raiders, where he started four games and compiled 25 tackles (10 solo), 1.0 tackle for loss and two passes defensed. news Colts activate tight end Will Mallory from injured reserve The Colts announced the move Saturday. news Colts release wide receiver Darius Slayton The Colts announced the move Friday. news Colts elevate WR Nick Westbrook-Ikhine to active roster from practice squad; place DE Arden Key on IR The Colts made the roster moves Saturday ahead of Week 5 against the Pittsburgh Steelers. news Colts sign DE Carl Lawson to practice squad, release TE Kenny Fletcher Jr. from practice squad The Colts made the roster move on Wednesday. The Dallas Cowboys entered Thursday night’s showdown with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers as 9.5-point favorites, yet they lost outright at home, destroying plenty of Survivor entries in the process. Week 5 had three teams that were obvious Survivor selections: Dallas, Houston and Cincinnati. They were all playing 0-4 teams, but only the Bengals and Texans came through. Luckily for the SI Betting team, neither of our editors selected the Cowboys this week, meaning that if you tailed our picks , you’re still alive heading into Week 6. Bye weeks are really starting to come into play in Survivor, as the Detroit Lions, Minnesota Vikings, Miami Dolphins and Bengals all won’t play in Week 6. One of the best strategies in Survivor this season has been fading the 0-5 Dolphins, so players will have to look elsewhere on Sunday. There are still some huge favorites in Week 6, the Los Angeles Rams are favored by double digits at home against the Arizona Cardinals, and the Kansas City Chiefs, Indianapolis Colts and New England Patriots are all favored by at least a touchdown at home. Each week, the SI Betting team of Iain MacMillan and Peter Dewey makes their favorite Survivor selections each week to help guide our readers through the season. Here’s a recap of our Week 5 selections before we dive into our favorite Survivor teams in Week 6. NFL Week 5 Survivor Picks Recap Peter Dewey: Cincinnati Bengals (W) Iain MacMillan: Houston Texans (W) Both Dewey and MacMillan faded winless teams in Week 5, and both wins were relatively sweat free with the Texans blowing out Tennessee and Cincy cruising to a big lead in a seven-point win over Miami. There are still plenty of playoff contenders that we can choose from in Week 6, even in just a 14-game slate. Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook NFL Week 6 Survivor Pool Picks Indianapolis Colts Indianapolis is going to be a popular pick in Survivor this week because it’s playing the Titans, but I’m willing to take a shot on Daniel Jones and company to get back to .500 at 3-3, especially at home. Indy is currently a seven-point favorite against the worst team in the AFC South. Cam Ward and the Titans have been downright awful on offense, ranking dead last in yards per play, 31st in EPA/Play and 26th in success rate during their 0-5 start. They’ve scored 20 or fewer points in every game, including three games where they scored 10 or less points. Indianapolis hasn’t done a great job of finishing drives this season, but it has one of the best kickers in the NFL in Spencer Shrader. So, Indy is able to get enough points on the board (like it did in Week 5) even if it doesn’t score a bunch of touchdowns. The Colts are allowing the third-most yards per play in the NFL on defense, which is a concern for them when it comes to this pick. However, Tennessee is 2-8 on the road in the Ward era, and it has covered the spread in just four of those games. The Indy offense isn’t a juggernaut, but it has moved the ball a lot better than the Titans, hanging 30 points on the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 2 while ranking 21st in success rate and 22nd in EPA/Play. I don’t see many spots where I’d willingly take the Colts in Survivor, so this is a way to use them and hopefully advance to Week 7. With more bye weeks ahead, it’s important to save a few top teams – if possible – for a game that may not be as much of a sure thing. Indy at home against the Titans is by far the most favorable game on the team’s schedule outside of a Nov. 15 home game against Miami. The Titans have been lost to open this season, and I don’t expect them to turn things around any time soon with how abysmal their offense has looked. The Colts may not cover, but they should handle business at home in Week 6. – Peter Dewey New England Patriots The New England Patriots proved last week that they still can show flashes of the team that won the AFC last season, especially when they play the weaker teams in the NFL. Their defense is a top 10 unit and Drake Maye can still torch a below average secondary. The Patriots now rank 10th in EPA per play, while the New York Jets rank 20th. New England is also 11th in opponent success rate, while New York is 23rd. That could all lead to big things for the Patriots in this divisional game. The Patriots have a ton of tough games on their schedule this season, including the Detroit Lions, Buffalo Bills, Kansas City Chiefs and Denver Broncos, so taking them when they're at home against either the Jets or Dolphins is going to be the move, which is why this is the week I'll take them at Gillette Stadium against Geno Smith and Aaron Glenn. Plus, New England is 18-2 at home in its last 20 games against the Jets. – Iain MacMillan Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. The New England Patriots (-7.5) will look to make it three straight wins when they host the New York Jets at Gillette Stadium on Sunday afternoon. New York and New England both boast defenses that can keep opposing offenses in check, so I'm taking the Under in my Jets vs. Patriots prediction . Keep reading to see all my free NFL picks for Sunday, Oct. 18. TOP Pick Jets vs Patriots prediction: Under 43.5 The New York Jets may be better than their 2-3 record suggests, but only because of their defense. The Jets offense averages 5.1 yards per play, 22nd in the NFL, and ranks 28th in scoring at 18.6 ppg. Brown coming off IR ALCS Game 4 postponed Defense will win WNBA Finals Jets vs. Patriots bold predictions for NFL Week 6 Mandatory Credit: David Butler II-Imagn Images Steve Silverman, ClutchPoints Tue, October 13, 2026 at 5:11 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New England Patriots and New York Jets are both fighting to get their season back on track and both appear to be making progress. The Patriots lost two of their first three games and appeared to be in serious trouble when they got blown out 35-6 by the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 3. Instead of playing like a potential MVP, quarterback Drake Maye had grown skittish and was making mistakes. In addition to throwing interceptions — he has already thrown 7 this season — he appeared to be losing his grip for a team with very high expectations. However, those writing off the Patriots or questioning their quarterback were premature. Maye has bounced back with two excellent games in key victories over the Bills and Raiders. While there are no guarantees in the NFL, the Patriots appear to be back on track and Maye appears to be regaining the momentum he had a year ago when the Pats host the Jets in Week 6. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Aaron Glenn had a very rough season in his first year as Jets head coach, but the defense appears to be very competitive in Year 2. The Jets have an alert and aggressive defense and that is enough to keep them competitive in most situations. The presence of Geno Smith under center represents an improvement over the situation a year ago when the Jets had inconsistent Justin Fields as their quarterback. Getting the best of the Patriots on their homefield would appear to be a major reach for the Jets. However, they were able to close out the Browns under difficult circumstances in Week 5, so they should go into the game with some confidence. Maye will go after the Jets secondary and throw for 250 yards and 2 TDs Maye turned his season around by leading the Patriots to a 29-26 upset in Week 4 against the explosive Bills. The quarterback completed 22 of 37 passes for 269 yards with 3 TDs and 1 interception and also ran for 54 yards. He followed up on that performance with an MVP-level game against the Raiders. Maye threw for 374 yards with 4 TDs and no interception and he also ran for a TD in a 45-17 blowout. There is little doubt that Maye is a better and more confident QB1 than he was after the loss to the Jaguars. However, the one thing that Maye knows is that head coach Mike Vrabel is not satisfied. "Today's not going to matter here in about 10 minutes," he said , per The Athletic. "We still have a lot to improve and to clean up. I'm happy but there's just a lot of things that we have to do to improve." The Jets have the fourth-ranked defense in the NFL, as they are giving up 293.0 yards per game. Glenn has an athletic, hard-hitting unit that will press the Patriots offense hard, and Maye will have to be aware of David Bailey. The rookie edge rusher from Texas Tech has 25 tackles, 5.0 sacks, 6 tackles for loss, 1 forced fumble and 1 pass defensed. He is a game-changing player and the Patriots will have to make sure he can't get too close to Maye. Geno Smith can pierce the Patriots defense with 250 yards and 2 TDs Mandatory Credit: Brad Penner-Imagn Images The Jets know that Smith is an accurate passer. As they head into this Week 6 matchup, Smith has completed 102 of 147 passes for 1,084 yards with 6 touchdowns and he has not thrown an interception. He has a solid go-to receiver in Garrett Wilson, and it will be a challenge for the Patriots to keep him in check. Wilson has caught 31 passes for 374 yards and has been on the receiving end of 3 of Smith's TD passes. The Patriots have one of the best cover men in the NFL in CB Christian Gonzalez. He will attempt to stop Wilson — or at least prevent him from making any big plays that change the momentum in the game. The key for the Jets in this game may be their ability to maintain possession and not give Maye the opportunity to torch them with big plays. They need running back Braelon Allen to have a big game. He scored the game-winning TD against the Brown with a 22-yard TD run late in the fourth quarter. If he can run for 65-70 yards in this game, it could take a lot of the pressure off of Smith and help him lead the offense to a competitive effort in this game. Jets will hang close in this game, but Pats emerge with tight victory The Jets are a better team than they were last year when they finished the season with a 3-14 record and were a last-place team in the AFC East. They will come into this game with confidence and they should be able to battle the Patriots closely for nearly 60 minutes. However, the Patriots have figured out how to win after their slow start, and Maye will come through in the late stages of the game to get the win in front of the home crowd. The Jets should not be discouraged because they have winnable games coming up against the struggling Dolphins and the Raiders. If they can win both of those games, the Jets will be a .500 team as they head into November. That's significant progress over last year's team and something for Glenn and Smith to build on. Brown coming off IR ALCS Game 4 postponed Defense will win WNBA Finals Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Chris Olave has been the one part of the Saints' offense nobody in the French Quarter is complaining about. The problem Sunday is that the New York Giants have a safety who has spent the season taking the ball away, and Jevon Holland will be waiting on every deep throw Tyler Shough sends Olave's way at MetLife Stadium. We noted this week that Olave is playing at an elite level , and it hasn't been close. Olave has 537 receiving yards, second in the NFL, and he's run 205 routes, more than any receiver in the league, according to PFF . His 89.4 overall grade ranks eighth among 86 qualifying wideouts, and his average depth of target sits at 13.4 yards. That's a lot of downfield work for a receiver who played through a foot scare against Minnesota. Holland is the league leader in interceptions with three, and he picked one off in each of the first three weeks, earning NFC Defensive Player of the Month honors for September. He's allowed just three receptions and a 40.8 passer rating in coverage, with an 86.3 overall grade that ranks fourth among 96 safeties, per PFF . He also has two forced fumbles. Where the Olave-Holland duel will be decided Sep 20, 2026; Baltimore, Maryland, USA; New Orleans Saints wide receiver Chris Olave (12) looks on from the sideline in the second quarter against the Baltimore Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jamie Sabau-Imagn ImagesJamie Sabau-Imagn Images Olave won't see Holland on every snap, since Holland plays deep and Olave works outside. The collision comes on the throws that define Olave's season: the deep crossers and go routes where Shough has to trust his receiver to win late. Giants coach John Harbaugh already knows it. "Those two guys, they're a connection right now," he said of Shough and Olave in the AP preview . That connection is also where Shough's mistakes have shown up. Shough has five interceptions on 205 attempts and called one of his picks against Minnesota "a stupid decision," as we wrote earlier this week . Holland made his name in Week 3 by sealing a win over Tennessee with an interception on the penultimate play . "This defense is definitely very sound," Holland said after earning the monthly award . If the Giants' blitzers force Shough to hurry, Holland gets more chances to read the quarterback's eyes and jump a route meant for Olave. Olave's status is worth watching, too. He missed practice early in the week with an illness and is listed as questionable . If he plays and wins two or three of those deep shots without feeding Holland a fourth pick, the Saints have a real path to snapping a three-game losing streak in New Jersey. away.headline: Saints Week 6 injury report vs. Giants: With Chris Olave ill, who is worth a fantasy football waiver pickup?
away.blurb: Chris Olave ’s illness creates late-week uncertainty for fantasy managers, but his return to practice suggests he is trending toward playing against the New York Giants . If Olave is ultimately ruled out, Saints receiver Devaughn Vele would become the best immediate replacement, while Germie Bernard and Tre Tucker offer stronger alternatives for managers searching beyond New Orleans. Olave did not practice Wednesday or Thursday before returning as a limited participant Friday. The Saints officially listed him as questionable, giving him a realistic chance to play but leaving fantasy managers without a definitive answer entering the weekend. If active, Olave should remain in starting lineups because of his featured role and favorable fantasy ceiling. New Orleans also listed Alvin Kamara as questionable with a back injury after three limited practices. Kamara’s status matters for the entire offense because his absence could force the Saints to lean more heavily on their passing game. Quarterback Tyler Shough practiced fully all week despite a left-hand issue and carries no game designation. Defensively, linebackers Kaden Elliss and Anfernee Jennings are out after missing every practice with calf and knee injuries, respectively. Defensive tackle Nathan Shepherd, defensive back Lorenzo Styles Jr. and long snapper Zach Wood join Olave and Kamara as questionable. Vernon Broughton, Tyree Wilson and Colby Wooden avoided final designations after improving during the week. Fantasy managers should monitor Sunday morning reports because New Orleans visits the Giants in the early window. Olave’s limited Friday practice is encouraging, but illness can affect conditioning and snap volume even when a player is cleared. Managers relying on him should have Vele or another early-game receiver available as insurance. Vele would project as New Orleans’ top available wide receiver without Olave, increasing his chances of leading the team in targets. He already carries flex value with Olave available and would move into low-end WR2 territory if the Saints deactivate their No. 1 receiver. His Week 5 line of four catches for 26 yards was disappointing, but he has scored at least 11.4 PPR points in three of five games. Bernard is a reasonable PPR flex against Tampa Bay, particularly for managers who miss out on Vele. His production remains less established, however, as he has 13 receptions for 140 yards without a touchdown this season. The waiver order is Vele, Bernard then Tucker. Start Vele confidently if Olave is ruled out, consider Bernard a PPR flex and use Tucker when chasing ceiling. If Olave plays, Vele remains usable, but his projection settles closer to flex range. home.headline: Saints Week 6 injury report vs. Giants: With Chris Olave ill, who is worth a fantasy football waiver pickup?
home.blurb: Chris Olave ’s illness creates late-week uncertainty for fantasy managers, but his return to practice suggests he is trending toward playing against the New York Giants . If Olave is ultimately ruled out, Saints receiver Devaughn Vele would become the best immediate replacement, while Germie Bernard and Tre Tucker offer stronger alternatives for managers searching beyond New Orleans. Olave did not practice Wednesday or Thursday before returning as a limited participant Friday. The Saints officially listed him as questionable, giving him a realistic chance to play but leaving fantasy managers without a definitive answer entering the weekend. If active, Olave should remain in starting lineups because of his featured role and favorable fantasy ceiling. New Orleans also listed Alvin Kamara as questionable with a back injury after three limited practices. Kamara’s status matters for the entire offense because his absence could force the Saints to lean more heavily on their passing game. Quarterback Tyler Shough practiced fully all week despite a left-hand issue and carries no game designation. Defensively, linebackers Kaden Elliss and Anfernee Jennings are out after missing every practice with calf and knee injuries, respectively. Defensive tackle Nathan Shepherd, defensive back Lorenzo Styles Jr. and long snapper Zach Wood join Olave and Kamara as questionable. Vernon Broughton, Tyree Wilson and Colby Wooden avoided final designations after improving during the week. Fantasy managers should monitor Sunday morning reports because New Orleans visits the Giants in the early window. Olave’s limited Friday practice is encouraging, but illness can affect conditioning and snap volume even when a player is cleared. Managers relying on him should have Vele or another early-game receiver available as insurance. Vele would project as New Orleans’ top available wide receiver without Olave, increasing his chances of leading the team in targets. He already carries flex value with Olave available and would move into low-end WR2 territory if the Saints deactivate their No. 1 receiver. His Week 5 line of four catches for 26 yards was disappointing, but he has scored at least 11.4 PPR points in three of five games. Bernard is a reasonable PPR flex against Tampa Bay, particularly for managers who miss out on Vele. His production remains less established, however, as he has 13 receptions for 140 yards without a touchdown this season. The waiver order is Vele, Bernard then Tucker. Start Vele confidently if Olave is ruled out, consider Bernard a PPR flex and use Tucker when chasing ceiling. If Olave plays, Vele remains usable, but his projection settles closer to flex range. home.headline: Saints Injury Report: Olave Questionable as Giants Face Offensive Line Concerns
home.blurb: Saints Injury Report: Olave Questionable as Giants Face Offensive Line Concerns Skip to main content SI.COM The Saints' top receiving target, Chris Olave , who missed the last two practices with an illness, was a limited participant Friday. If Olave can play Sunday, starting quarterback Tyler Shough can breathe a sigh of relief. On defense, linebacker Kaden Elliss and edge rusher Anfernee Jennings are out again for Sunday. As for the Giants, edge rusher Abdul Carter and starting offensive tackles Jermaine Eluemunor and Andrew Thomas have been listed as questionable. LB Anfernee Jennings: Out (knee) RB Alvin Kamara: Questionable (back) WR Chris Olave: Questionable (illness) DT Nathan Shepherd: Questionable (illness) CB Lorenzo Styles: Questionable (knee) LS Zach Wood: Questionable (calf) LB Abdul Carter: Questionable (calf) T Andrew Thomas: Questionable (groin) T Jermaine Eluemunor: Questionable (calf) CB Colton Hood: Out (concussion) As pressure mounts around the organization , the New Orleans Saints look to end their losing skid and get back on track on the road against the New York Giants on Sunday, but concerns linger over their latest injury report. Olave has recorded 39 catches for 537 yards with a touchdown. Olave is second in the league in receiving yards and is tied for third in receptions. Elliss, who is arguably the Saints’ best player at his position, has been greatly missed as the Saints have allowed 179 yards per game on the ground since his injury during their 35-27 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 3. Concerns about Season Reach the Top After Saints owner Gayle Benson said the Saints’ 1-4 start was “unacceptable” earlier in the week, head coach Kellen Moore said after practice he speaks with her regularly and communicated with her throughout the week. "We're all just trying to reach the same goal," Moore said. "We all want to win football games, and so we're all working toward that." The availability of both Eluemunor and Thomas could have major implications for Sunday's matchup, particularly against a solid edge rusher rotation of New Orleans’ Carl Granderson , Chase Young and Cameron Jordan .
