I have four underdogs not only finding their way into my five locks of the week, but also two of them pulling off outright upsets. Judging by the headline of this article, you already know that the Panthers are one of those dogs that I think will win in Week 6 as they head up to Philly to face the Eagles . While I'll get into why I feel that way below, I'm just as fascinated by what may happen if it comes to fruition. Would this be the straw that breaks the camel's back when it comes to Nick Sirianni's job? Or does he live to fight another day and gear up for a do-or-die NFC East showdown in primetime with the Cowboys in Week 7? Either way, the storylines that could flow out of this upcoming slate feel like they're as juicy as we've seen so far this season, and that's saying something. Anyways, I'll look to improve upon my picks after a lackluster Week 5 where I went 2-3 ATS with my five locks of the week, along with 6-9 ATS and 9-5-1 SU for the overall slate. Note : Cincinnati, Detroit, Miami and Minnesota are on the bye in Week 6. Locks of the Week ATS : 12-12-1 ATS : 33-44-2 Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles Sunday, 1 p.m. (CBS, Stream on Paramount+ ) Carolina comes into this matchup with a pretty sizable rest advantage over Philadelphia. On top of the Panthers coming off of the bye, the Eagles were just in London last week. So, we have one team extremely well rested, while the other is reeling and just came off a demoralizing international loss. Beyond the lopsided rest advantage, the Eagles just feel like a mess right now. They're bottom five in the league in points per game (18.4), yards per game (262.2), and passing yards per game (170.6) coming into Week 6. Sure, some of that can be attributed to injury, but even when they've had their full squad, it's been clunky. Conversely, Carolina's offense is top-five in the NFL in those same categories, and it looks like they'll get No. 2 wideout Jalen Coker back for this one. I like the Panthers to roll into Lincoln Financial Field and turn the heat up under Nick Sirianni's seat to a fever pitch. Projected score: Panthers 23, Eagles 21 The pick: Panthers +1.5 Pittsburgh Steelers at Tampa Bay Buccaneers This is another game that has some outliers worth targeting. The Bucs will be at home after an upset win over the Cowboys last Thursday night in Dallas. They'll have the rest advantage over a Steelers team that took care of business against the Colts on Sunday. Similar to how I think the Cowboys sort of overlooked the then-winless Buccaneers with an undrafted rookie quarterback under center, Pittsburgh could get caught sleeping here, too. Not so much because they're going to overlook Jalon Daniels , but the Steelers could get caught looking ahead to their Week 7 matchup against the Saints in Paris. With a France trip on the horizon for Pittsburgh, I think Tampa Bay is a live home dog. Moreover, I think the Bucs defense has a good shot at containing the Steelers offense. Tampa Bay is allowing the second-fewest rushing yards per game in the NFL through Week 5, which could limit Jaylen Warren's impact. Meanwhile, Todd Bowles has some solid splits against Aaron Rodgers over the course of his career as both a head coach and defensive coordinator. Rodgers' teams are 1-2 against Bowles and average just 16.7 points per game. Projected score: Buccaneers 24, Steelers 23 The pick: Buccaneers +3 Tennessee Titans at Indianapolis Colts Sunday, 1 p.m. (Fox, Stream: Fubo , try for free) You'll undoubtedly scratch your head at this pick, and it's hard to blame you. Tennessee hasn't instilled any confidence this season and is punting on a league-high 53% of its drives. Still, I think this line is too big in a divisional matchup against the Colts, whom I don't believe are a serious player in the AFC. The Indy offense can't move the ball efficiently, ranking 29th in the NFL in yards per play (4.6). Meanwhile, their defense is 28th in the league in total yards allowed (384.2). Daniel Jones has also turned the ball over more times (7) than he's found the end zone (4) this season. So, for as bad as the Titans offense has been this season, Indy isn't that far off, so I'll gladly put the full touchdown in my back pocket. Projected score: Colts 24, Titans 20 The pick: Titans +7 Arizona Cardinals at Los Angeles Rams Sunday, 4:05 p.m. (Fox, Stream: Fubo , try for free) I think we're firmly on backdoor alert with this line. L.A. is coming off an overtime loss to the Bills on Monday night, so this is quite the turnaround for Sean McVay's club. Matthew Stafford dropped back and threw 54 times in the loss, while the Rams offense ran 78 total plays. That could see them a bit sluggish in this contest. I don't envision Arizona pulling off the upset, but I do think they're capable of scoring late to get us within the number here. For instance, Arizona kept the offense on the field throughout a blowout loss to Detroit and scored a largely meaningless touchdown just before the two-minute warning. That's the type of play we'll be looking for them here. Projected score: Rams 30, Cardinals 17 The pick: Cardinals +13.5 New York Jets at New England Patriots I think the Patriots are all the way back. Drake Maye has seemingly returned to his MVP form from last year and just tallied five touchdowns in a blowout win over the Raiders . Gillette Stadium has been a comfortable spot for New England as they're 10-1 in their last 11 home games. Meanwhile, they've also taken care of business against inferior opponents under Mike Vrabel as the Patriots are 11-0 with him at the helm when facing teams entering with a losing record. Further looking at the trends for this one, the Patriots are 12-0 straight-up and 10-2 ATS in their last 12 games as a favorite and have a +17.9 PPG differential over that stretch. As for the Jets , they've yet to win or cover (0-6) a divisional game under head coach Aaron Glenn. The latest odds I saw post-Week 5 on the first NFL head coach fired had Washington's Dan Quinn as the +200 favorite and Sirianni next at +400. And that's absolutely no surprise to me after both NFC East head coaches made utterly stupid decisions that cost their teams victories this past Sunday. I'm sure you know by know what happened in Commanders-Giants and Eagles-Jaguars. Quinn and/or Jayden Daniels didn't even get a field-goal try off at end of overtime, with a win in Washington's hands. Maybe that clock mistake was on Daniels, but there's no doubt it's on Sirianni for having Jake Elliott kick off into the Jacksonville landing zone on Sunday in London. That allowed a long return and a walk-off 57-yard field goal to win. All the Eagles had to do was kick the ball out of the end zone and the Jags are at their 35 hoping for a Hail Mary with no timeouts. Kudos to Sirianni for taking the blame, but he wouldn't take any for managing the prior scoring drive in a way that left the Jaguars with more time than they should have had. Two passes stopped the clock, and Elliott kicked the go-ahead field goal with 12 seconds left. Why not run it down to only a couple and make that the final play? "I'm honoring a play call, honoring the things that are coming in the game," QB Jalen Hurts said afterward. "We're not asking him to make play calls in that scenario," Sirianni responded to Monday. Starting to feel a disconnect there? The Eagles' next game is on a bit of extra rest, as it is Monday night in Week 7 vs. Dallas, so you might see a change if this goes badly Sunday, even though Sirianni is 67-33 as the Eagles head coach. That's tied for the fifth-best head coaching record through 100 games in the league since 1970. The team's bye isn't until Week 10, and you can already hear the Mike Tomlin rumors. This marks Sirianni's third three-game losing streak in Philadelphia, and he has never lost four in a row. It's not just his clock management, but his offense has been lousy during this skid in averaging 14.7 points and 217 yards per game while converting just 22.2% of third downs. With Lane Johnson having retired, Cam Jurgens traded and Landon Dickerson on injured reserve, the team has replaced three starters already. And it's not clear yet if the offense will have tailback and former NFL Offensive Player of the Year Saquon Barkley and No. 1 wideout DeVonta Smith back from injury yet, after both missed Week 5. The Eagles are averaging a scant 3.5 yards per play with both off the field this season, compared to 5.3 in all other situations. It's possible the Eagles are down to their No. 4 tailback because No. 2 Tank Bigsby is on IR and No. 3 Will Shipley was hurt against the Jags. This will mark the first time the Eagles will take the field sitting below .500 since 2021, when they were 6-7. The 76 straight games played without a losing record was the longest streak in team history. The overall NFL record is 145 by the Patriots from 2003-12. Carolina comes off its bye with its 2-2 mark the team's best four-game start since 2021. It's also good enough for the lead in the ultra-weak NFC South – the Panthers are +130 favorites. We get a former all-Alabama quarterback matchup here in Bryce Young vs. Hurts with Young off to his best start and perhaps answering all those lingering questions that have dogged the former No. 1 overall pick. Thanks to Young and sensational second-year wideout Tetairoa McMillan , the Panthers rank top five in the league in scoring offense (30.3 PPG), total offense (405.8 YPG) and passing offense (301.3 YPG). The scoring average is the best in franchise history through four games, and it's their first time averaging at least 30.0 PPG in any four-game span since 2019. Young would make history if he keeps his NFL-best 317.0-yard passing average up, as no QB ever has averaged even 275 yards passing in a season after three straight years under 200.0 passing yards per. Young also led the NFL entering his bye week with 11 completions on deep throws (20+ air yards). He is 0-1 against Hurts in the NFL as the Eagles beat the visiting Panthers 22-16 in the most recent meeting in December 2024. away.blurb: Jalen Hurts has already been confirmed out for the Week 6 showdown, putting Tanner McKee in the role as the Eagles' starting QB. But each of the last two weeks, he has had to sit out. If Smith is out, the Panthers will have to be prepared for a number of different possibilities — just because the Eagles will mix and match WR roles to fit the situation at hand. The first-round rookie Makai Lemon will be out there, too, and he's a dangerous playmaker. Beyond that trio, the Eagles also have possession receiver Elijah Moore and a guy used mostly in the return game, Britain Covey. The Panthers are going to face a shorthanded Eagles team either way. But if Smith is out, too, the pendulum shifts even more in Carolina's favor. away.blurb: Carolina Panthers Injury Update: 2 Key Players Gearing up for Their Return - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Carolina Panthers Injury Update: 2 Key Players Gearing up for Their Return Fans of the Carolina Panthers have finally got some good news regarding injuries. For the past four weeks, whenever the injury banner pops up in their feed, Carolina Panthers fans have covered and resigned, expecting to see their favorite player out for an extended period of time. However, this week, Dave Canales spoke to the media with updates on Taylor Moton and Tershawn Wharton . Wharton had neck surgery back in May, also putting him on an unknown timetable for his return. He was immediately placed on the PUP list, and the Panthers have tried to fill his role as the interior speed rusher. While there has been some success with Pat Jones, who has also missed time, there has been limited production elsewhere. Rookie Lee Hunter has so far been the most effective defensive tackle next to Derrick Brown, but on obvious passing downs, his slow pass rush has been a hindrance at times. In the same press conference where coach Canales revealed that Moton and wharton's windows were open, he also revealed the fate of Trevor Etienne, who began the season on IR. Etienne injured his knee during the final roster cutdowns, allowing Carolina to keep an open roster slot while placing him on IR. He is now ready to make his return. While his production was limited in his rookie season, sitting behind Rico Dowdle and Chuba Hubbard, Etienne played well with special teams and passing situations for Carolina down the stretch in 2025. In a year where the Panthers again lost Johanthan Brooks to am extend groin injury, getting Etienne back to give Carolina running back room of three backs allows for Hubbard and Dillon to get much need resort during games, as well as a buffer in anymore unexpected injuries happen. Etienne will most likely return to his role in special teams, giving Carolina another player with kick and punt return experience to work with. The Carolina Panthers have been an injury riddle in the 2026 season. An early bye week came bearing fruit for the Panthers' injury news. Taylor Moton and Tershawn Wharton's return spells good things on the horizon for Carolina. Moton will allow Freeling to return to the development pool, allowing him to review his film, watch a Panthers staple on the right side, and learn from him. It will also give Freeling a chance to get healthier himself, after suffering a concussion and a knee injury in the last two weeks. Wharton's return means that Carolina might get a boost in pass rush. Wharton has always had the speed and strength to work from the inside, and adding him to a room with Jaelan Phillips and Princely Umanmielen means Carolina will have a perfect blend of speed and power. home.blurb: Earlier this week, stunning news arrived that Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts was ruled out for Sunday’s game against the Carolina Panthers due to a superficial blood clot discovered before the team’s London game earlier this month. He’s been receiving treatment for the superficial blood clot, also known as superficial thrombophlebitis , and practiced fully this past Wednesday ahead of the Panthers game. However, the team revealed that new ultrasound findings led to him being ruled out for Sunday’s game. “On Wednesday night, a follow-up ultrasound revealed movement in the small blood clot. Jalen will be out for Sunday’s game vs. the Panthers as we determine the appropriate course of treatment. His health and safety are our highest priority,” the team’s statement said on Thursday. “Michael Robinson is accusing Jalen Hurts of saying, ‘Well if everybody’s hurt, I’m hurt, too.’ And that Jalen Hurts is ‘pulling himself out so that this doesn’t look like it’s on me.’ when Jalen Hurts has a BLOOD CLOT THAT SHOWED MOVEMENT AND COULD BE LIFE THREATENING,” Griffin III wrote. Griffin III hasn’t played since the Baltimore Ravens released him in early 2021 and has since moved into podcasting and appearances on various Fox Sports programs to share his insights. His calling out of Robinson on X made clear that he believes Hurts’ health takes priority over criticism of the Eagles quarterback and the team’s struggles. ESPN’s Tim McManus reported that Hurts was a full participant in Eagles practice last Friday ahead of the Sunday matchup in London against the Jacksonville Jaguars. He then “played without limitation” in that game, which the Eagles lost, 19-17. Amid the concerning health issue Hurts is experiencing, former Seattle Seahawks and San Francisco 49ers fullback Michael Robinson shared a controversial take on NFL Network’s “NFL Gameday.” He suggested, while playing “devil’s advocate,” that with the Eagles potentially linking their struggles to Hurts, he could be using the injury to distance himself from that blame. The Pittsburgh Steelers are currently 2.5-point favorites for their Week 6 road game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. However, NFL analyst Conor Orr thinks the oddsmakers have it completely wrong. Orr predicts the Steelers will continue their hot streak and dominate the Buccaneers in Week 6. "I wanna see the Steelers go down to Tampa Bay and win another one of these games," Orr said . "I think they can win this game by three touchdowns." Orr has done a complete 180 in just a matter of a week. Heading into Week 5, he begged the Indianapolis Colts to put the Steelers out of their misery. "Clearly you have communication issues. Your coach came out and said your house is dirty and you need to clean your house. Something's a mess here," Orr said on the Heed the Call NFL Podcast . "I'm sick of [Aaron Rodgers]. I'm sick of watching this team. I'm sick of the receivers dropping balls. I'm sick of them having played one good game against the Bengals so we've got to take them seriously for another three weeks. Come on, Jonathan Taylor. Put up 400 yards and put his old, dying horse out of its misery and off my screen." However, after watching the Steelers offense come alive in their latest win, Orr issued an apology to the team and now seems to be a big believer in Pittsburgh. "I have totally done a 180, and I'll admit it, on this Steelers offense," Orr continued. "Down so many people, and even down to Ben Skowronek, this team has been able to find a way to manufacture points. Aaron Rodgers will have bad Rodgers games, but I've totally flipped on this." The Steelers do seem to have some new found life. Rodgers is playing very well and running back Jaylen Warren has been on another level, recording 176, 126 and 188-yard performances the past three weeks. The only question that remains is: Can the Steelers offense continue this type of production the rest of the season? away.headline: Steelers get brutal Roman Wilson injury news right before Week 6
away.blurb: This Steelers offense has looked good at times this season, especially with rookie second-rounder Germie Bernard recently breaking out. But another young breakout wide receiver recently got some bad news. Roman Wilson was ruled out for Week 6's matchup early in the week, and unfortunately, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter , the Steelers have placed Wilson on injured reserve before Week 6, meaning he's out for the next four games. Wilson, dealing with a finger injury, is now going to miss a lot more than just Week 6 for the Steelers. He's now out for at least four games due to this IR news. With a Week 9 bye, the earliest Wilson could return for the Steelers is in Week 11, when they face the Philadelphia Eagles . But with his finger injury landing him on IR, Wilson is going to be out through at least Week 10 this season for Pittsburgh. away.headline: Steelers injury report: Pittsburgh enters road trip with abundance of injuries
away.blurb: Out of the bye, road trips to face the division rival Bengals and in-state rival Eagles await. Neither is a long trip in terms of mileage, but the Steelers have not won in Philadelphia since 1965, and it follows an AFC North dogfight. The receivers room is the most pressing problem. Pittman will be out for at least the next three games after being placed on injured reserve. The veteran was a key offseason acquisition but has only played in three games in which he's caught seven passes for 89 yards. The extent of the injuries to Wilson and Skowronek, sustained against Indianapolis, are not yet known, but McCarthy said Monday that both will be out for at least the Tampa Bay game. The secondary is a bit better off. Ramsey spent the week leading up to the Colts game on the injury report but handled a normal workload. Only Dean was absent, and the Steelers have not yet taken the step of adding the free agent cornerback signing to injured reserve. Dean was a limited practice participant Wednesday while Ramsey was out with a wrist injury listed. McCarthy hinted strongly that Dowdle is expected back this week from the toe injury he sustained in Week 2 against New England. He was also limited Wednesday. That should help the offense manage the reps of Jaylen Warren, who's handled a heavy workload in Dowdle's absence. away.blurb: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have released their final injury report ahead of Sunday's Week 6 matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers, and several key players will be unavailable as Tampa Bay looks to build on last week's victory over Dallas. Rookie Jalon Daniels will make his third consecutive start after leading the Buccaneers to their first victory of the season last Thursday against the Cowboys. The Buccaneers will also be without safety Antoine Winfield Jr. (rib), who did not participate in practice throughout the week. Wide receiver David Sills V (hamstring) was also ruled out despite being listed as a full participant in all three practices. Cornerback Benjamin Morrison (quad) is listed as doubtful, while linebackers SirVocea Dennis (ankle/foot) and Josiah Trotter (knee), cornerback Ayden Garnes (ankle), and running back Sean Tucker (quad) are questionable. Dennis and Garnes were full participants Friday, providing some encouraging news heading into the weekend. Pittsburgh is also dealing with several injuries, particularly at wide receiver. Roman Wilson (finger) and Ben Skowronek (calf) have been ruled out, along with safety DeShon Elliott (knee). Wide receiver DK Metcalf was added to Friday's report with an illness and is questionable. home.headline: The Latest on Baker Mayfield’s Status for the Buccaneers
home.blurb: Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield will miss a third straight game in Week 6 as he continues to recover from a dislocated thumb, but his return could be close. Mayfield has not been able to return to full practice, and the Buccaneers are not rushing him back before he can throw comfortably. Head coach Todd Bowles said Mayfield attempted to throw earlier in the week, but swelling in the thumb remained an issue. His practice participation next week will be an important sign of whether he is ready to play. Daniels is expected to make his third consecutive start in Week 6 when Tampa Bay faces the Pittsburgh Steelers. The Buccaneers will need the rookie to manage the offense and avoid costly mistakes while Mayfield remains unavailable. A return against Carolina would give Tampa Bay its starting quarterback for a divisional matchup with importance. The Buccaneers have yet to face an NFC South opponent this season, so the Week 7 game offers an early chance to make ground within the division. home.headline: Baker Mayfield's potential return game for Buccaneers revealed
home.blurb: According to a report from NFL insider Tom Pelissero , the two-time Pro Bowl quarterback is aiming for a return to the lineup in Week 7 against the Carolina Panthers . That would be in time for the Buccaneers' first NFC South game of the season. "Bucs QB Baker Mayfield will miss a third consecutive game since dislocating his thumb in Week 3," said Pelissero. "But there’s optimism he’ll return next week — just in time for Tampa Bay’s first division game of the season at Carolina." The Buccaneers are 1-4 right now, but it's worth noting that the Panthers lead the division at just a 2-2 record. In other words, if Mayfield can return next week in a game against his former team -- he loves revenge games -- the Buccaneers still have plenty of time to improve and win this division. This article originally appeared on Bucs Wire: Baker Mayfield's potential return game for Buccaneers revealed The Tampa Bay Buccaneers may play the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 6 without Baker Mayfield, but it may be the last time they have to do so. Mayfield suffered the thumb injury at the end of the Buccaneers' Week 3 loss to the Minnesota Vikings . Tampa Bay has played the past two weeks without Mayfield, starting undrafted rookie free agent quarterback Jalon Daniels. The Buccaneers are 1-1 with Daniels as their starting quarterback, having won their most recent game against the Dallas Cowboys. Daniels has looked solid, with two touchdowns and three interceptions and a 69.1% completion rate. He's also contributed 87 rushing yards on 16 carries. Regardless, the Buccaneers will go with Mayfield when he's healthy. The two-time Pro Bowl quarterback signed a deal worth $55 million annually across three years for a total of $165 million. Prior to his injury, Mayfield had thrown two touchdowns against two interceptions for an 80.0 passer rating with a 63.5% completion rate.

picks.headline: Week 6 Preview: Arizona Cardinals vs Los Angeles Rams
picks.blurb: Week 6 Preview: Arizona Cardinals vs Los Angeles Rams - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Unranked Auburn shocks No. 1 Georgia on road TRENDING Fantasy Basketball Sign Up College football live updates A.J. Brown coming off IR ALCS Game 4 postponed Defense will win WNBA Finals Week 6 Preview: Arizona Cardinals vs Los Angeles Rams | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Michael Roberts, Editor Toussaint Fancher Sat, October 17, 2026 at 12:30 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads After a disappointing end to Week 5 , the Los Angeles Rams look to get back in the win column against the Arizona Cardinals. "I love Mike [LaFleur], and it's about the Rams versus the Cardinals, and we're going to try to get after him as good as we can this week," Rams head coach Sean McVay said about facing the Cardinals. The Rams will face the Cardinals in the first matchup against former Los Angeles offensive coordinator, Mike LaFleur. LaFleur spent the past two seasons as the Rams' offensive coordinator, and now they will face off for the first time since LaFleur became Arizona's head coach. Last week, the Los Angeles Rams had a great offensive game. The offense was electric as the game became a barnburner. Buffalo and their quarterback Josh Allen were unstoppable on the ground and got the best of the Los Angeles defense. This week, the Rams face the Arizona Cardinals, who are currently 1-4 and on a three-game losing streak. While the Rams must approach every game with the same level of preparation, the Cardinals are an easier opponent than the Bills. Although the Cardinals are an easier matchup, they still have plenty of playmakers. Michael Wilson, Jeremiyah Love and Trey McBride are a few of their top tier players who can change the game at a moment's notice. The Cardinals quarterback, Jacoby Brissett, is an experienced veteran who can play his best at any moment. Last season, the journeyman threw for over 3,300 yards with 23 touchdowns – both career highs. The Cardinals are a wildcard on any given game, but the Rams should be able to handle Arizona easily. Oct 12, 2026; Inglewood, California, USA; Los Angeles Rams place kicker Harrison Mevis (92) kicks a point after try during the fourth quarter against the Buffalo Bills at SoFi Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images After the Week 5 loss to the Bills, the Rams made big changes, specifically to the special teams unit. Rams released kicker Harrison Mevis after his poor performance. Mevis missed a 50-yard field attempt and also had a game leading 48-yard field goal blocked in overtime. Rams also released returner and wide receiver Xavier Smith – marred by his costly turnover in the NFC championship game last season. The Rams signed Blake Grupe off the New York Jets' practice squad as a replacement. Last season, he played for the Indianapolis Colts and the New Orleans Saints, going 29 for 37 with a long of 60 yards. The Rams' special teams has been the league's worst under McVay since he became head coach. McVay stood behind his special teams coordinator Bubba Ventrone after the loss. "I have a lot of confidence in Bubba Ventrone," said McVay on Tuesday. "There are no changes that are going to be made there. We're going to keep working. This isn't the first time that we've had adversity and the first time that we've had some different things that I have to do a better job of." Following Monday Night's game, the NFL suspended Rams starting left tackle Alaric Jackson for two games after he threw a punch at Bills edge rusher Bradley Chubb. Jackson appealed and his suspension was reduced to one game. Jackson will miss this week's matchup against the Cardinals before returning next week against the Las Vegas Raiders. While no players have been listed out for the game, several were on the injury report or missed practice this week. Tight end Davis Allen was listed as Did Not Participate (DNP) due to a foot injury, and Omar Speights, Nate Landman, Colby Parkinson and Kam Curl were all limited participants. The Last Word Even though the Rams are 2-3, they are still in a good place. The next five games are all winnable, they must remain focused on their opponent each week. The Rams have started 2-3 or worse in four of their six seasons with quarterback Matthew Stafford. In 2023, the Rams started 2-3 and the following year saw a 1-4 start. Despite the slow starts, the Rams made the playoffs in both seasons. The Rams are also waiting on the return of Myles Garrett to pair his extraordinary talents with Aaron Donald. The Rams still have a tough task ahead and need to focus on coming away with a victory on Sunday. away.headline: Arizona Cardinals' LaFleur announces Jeremiyah Love injury status
away.blurb: It is not yet clear whether Love’s injury will affect his availability in Week 7, when the Cardinals return home to face the Denver Broncos. When asked whether Love could be placed on injured reserve, LaFleur said “there’s been no discussion of IR or anything like that.” “He's doing good but it's just — you guys see the way he cuts,” LaFleur said. “He cuts hard. That's a superpower of his. And when he's putting his left foot in the ground, it's just not right, right now. And to get him to be to his best ability, it's what's right so he can go out and perform the way that he wants.” Earlier in the week, LaFleur said that Love’s limited involvement as a receiver was because the Cardinals needed their running backs to stay back in pass protection against the Lions. On Friday, he acknowledged that was only a partial truth. Amid a slow start to his rookie season, Love will miss the Arizona Cardinals ' Week 6 trip to face the Los Angeles Rams due to an injury to his left ankle, head coach Mike LaFleur said on Friday, Oct. 16. Love has not practiced all week after experiencing lingering discomfort in recent games. “We knew on Monday after watching the game, talking with him, seeing where he was at, that we were gonna give him Wednesday off,” LaFleur said. “And re-assess on Wednesday, with knowing that probably Sunday was a long shot.” “We've gotta really re-evaluate, really every single day,” LaFleur added. “Not good enough, obviously, right now to go Sunday. It wouldn't be in the best interest of him. And then we'll re-evaluate, obviously, on Monday.” Love suffered a high-ankle sprain to his right ankle on Aug. 13, in a preseason game against the Las Vegas Raiders. He returned to the field a month later in the Cardinals’ regular-season opener. Then, at some point in the ensuing weeks, he began to experience discomfort in his left ankle. The issue first drew public attention in Week 4, against the New York Giants. During that game, trainers repeatedly looked at Love’s ankle on the Cardinals sideline. Afterward, Love acknowledged that the Cardinals have been managing his workload due to health. LaFleur, though, was unsure of exactly when the issue first surfaced. "We just felt like it wasn't improving and maybe even getting a little bit worse," LaFleur said. "So at that point, if it's not improving and it's getting a little bit worse, we've gotta do what's right for the player." Through five games, Love has just 245 rushing yards on 67 carries, for a 3.7 yards per carry average. Love has also caught just 11 passes on 14 targets for 36 yards, falling far short of the expectations with he entered the NFL as a pass-catcher. Over the Cardinals’ past two games, he ran just 20 total routes. “To run routes and separate, you've gotta be able to put those feet in the ground,” LaFleur said. “And it's gotta be deliberate. home.headline: New Trent McDuffie injury could shake up Rams secondary yet again
home.blurb: For a second straight week, the Los Angeles Rams' final injury report is thankfully sparse. The headliner in Week 6 is star cornerback Trent McDuffie, a late addition after tweaking his groin in practice, per head coach Sean McVay. McDuffie sat out Friday's session and his status for Sunday's game against the Arizona Cardinals could be in jeopardy. Safety Kam Curl, another Friday DNP, is also questionable with an ankle injury, but McVay said he "feels good" about his status for the game. If McDuffie misses, that means more Josh Wallace and Emmanuel Forbes in coverage. Where have we heard that before? The Rams encountered a similar scenario with Jaylen Watson out for the second half in Week 3 against the Broncos and in Week 4 versus Philadelphia. In addition to Watson, the defense also played multiple games without safety Kamren Kinchens, who strained his hamstring in Week 1 and sat out until the Eagles game. Although Curl hasn't missed a game, he's been nursing that ankle injury all year. The other starting safety, Quentin Lake, was questionable entering Week 5 before suiting up to play. Wallace has played well and, based on how the Rams handled Watson's absence, would replace McDuffie as the second starter on the outside. Aside from a very poor showing in Denver, Forbes has also performed decently in limited reps. Relying on those two against Arizona would not be the end of the world. For whatever reason, this Rams secondary can't seem to stay healthy. Rams will call on Wallace and Forbes if Trent McDuffie misses McDuffie, one of the NFL's top corners this season, would be the biggest loss by far, and late injury-report additions tend to bode poorly. "He's got the right mentality and mindset and we'll kind of just see where we're at," McVay said of McDuffie's chances to play. The other part, of course, is that it's against Arizona , who just traded former first-round receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. and will also miss rookie running back Jeremiyah Love (ankle) this week against the Rams. The Cardinals' top receiving threat is tight end Trey McBride, which is more a problem for linebackers Nate Landman and Omar Speights and Lake as a nickel. McBride is only averaging 7.3 yards per catch, anyway, and Arizona's lead wideout Michael Wilson, while providing a productive 57.6 yards per contest, is averaging just 9.9. WR2 Kendrick Bourne might actually be the bigger concern for LA; with the San Francisco 49ers, meeting last season, an overtime win for 'Zona, Bourne erupted for 10 catches and 142 yards. ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals have a lengthy injury report entering this weekend's clash with the Los Angeles Rams. Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur dove deeper into Love's absence, which you can read about here . Off the Cardinals' injury report is all of Carson Beck (back), Devin Duvernay (ribs), Isaac Seumalo (rest) and Josh Sweat (rest). It's a familiar battle for both sides entering the week, as LaFleur spent the last few seasons under head coach Sean McVay in Los Angeles as the team's offensive coordinator, putting him against Rams defensive coordinator Chris Shula. "There's obviously familiarity with just going against him for two of the three years. home.headline: Jeremiyah Love Gets Concerning Injury Update Ahead of Cardinals-Rams
home.blurb: TEMPE — The Arizona Cardinals are holding star rookie running back Jeremiyah Love out of practice on Wednesday as Week 6 preperations for the Los Angeles Rams ramp up. Jeremiyah Love Gets Concerning Injury Update Ahead of Cardinals-Rams Skip to main content SI.COM "Take him one day at a time. You know, we want to get this ankle right and do it the right way," Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur told reporters on Wednesday. Love has been nursing an ankle injury through the opening stages of his rookie season after suffering a different ankle injury during preseason. While he hasn't missed any regular season action, Love's participation and impact has been slightly hindered. There's been some talks about potentially shutting Love down to allow the ankle to heal, though LaFleur didn't seem willing to do that. Arizona is just 1-4 and is again favored to lose in Los Angeles. "Listen, I'm going to try to be as candid as possible with also knowing that everyone's listening to this too, right? But he's a tough dude. You guys see the way he plays and how aggressive he is with his cuts. I mean, imagine being a running back in the NFL trying to put the foot down and cut the way that you know that you're capable of," LaFleur said. "And so we all are in agreeance — as much as you know he wants to battle through — we're all in agreeance right now, it's just hey, give [the injury] a little bit of rest and see as the week goes on, what that'll entail for Sunday." Love, the No. 3 overall pick, has 67 carries for 245 yards and one touchdown on the ground while adding 11 receptions for 36 yards and a score through the air. "I think early at his career [he battled injuries], but you had the right [ankle] early, and then now you got the left one. So now you're just kind of — it's just double dipping. The right side, the preseason one's fine. It's the other one right now that's the lingering issue. They're ankles, you know, it's an ankle. I'm not a doctor, and each body's a little bit different," LaFleur continued. "Like the way he came back from the one in the preseason was unbelievable, like he doesn't even feel it. But this one is the one that happened kind of when the regular season started, and it just lingered." Has Love lost any of his explosiveness? "You'd have to ask him that," LaFleur added. "I know how explosive he is. I know how explosive he wants to be. So I mean I think that's a fair assessment in some aspects. Again, I don't think it's an overall hindrance, but again the the rest for him is going to be vital." Justin Herbert and the Chargers have yet to win a game this season, going from a preseason darling to one of the worst teams in the NFL. Not only are the Chargers winless, but they have yet to cover the spread and rank in the bottom half of the league in almost every key metric. So, this isn’t a case of a tough schedule messing up L.A.’s playoff chances. Meanwhile, the Chiefs are undefeated and appear to be back in the mix for the No. 1 seed in the AFC after a six-win 2025 campaign. Kenneth Walker III has totally transformed a Kansas City offense that ranks in the top-10 in the league in EPA/Play, yards per play and success rate in 2026. Oddsmakers have set Mahomes and Co. as massive favorites at home in this AFC West clash, but can they cover? All season long, the SI Betting team is predicting the final score of every NFL game – a fun way to help bettors decide on their spread, moneyline and total bets. Plus, there’s a chance that we’ll hit an exact score in the process! This AFC West matchup has major implications for the Chiefs as they eye the No. 1 seed in the conference, especially since they already had their bye. Let’s dive right into the odds and my score prediction for Sunday’s game. Chargers vs. Chiefs Odds, Spread and Total Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Chargers +8.5 (-115) Chiefs -8.5 (-105) Chargers: +380 42.5 (Over -108/Under -112) The total in this matchup has dropped a point since open , but the Chiefs remain 8.5-point favorites at home against a Chargers team that has yet to get a win in 2026. Los Angeles is 0-4-1 against the spread after failing to cover against Denver in Week 5. Chargers vs. Chiefs Score Prediction SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan has taken on the challenge of betting on every NFL game this season in his Road to 272 column . Earlier this week, he explained why he’s taking the OVER in this matchup: Don't look now, but the Patrick Mahomes-led Chiefs once again have one of the best offenses in football. They lead the league in yards per play, averaging 6.5 yards per snap, and they also rank fourth in EPA per play and fifth in offensive success rate. Led by Offensive Player of the Year favorite Kenneth Walker, they're a dangerous offense to face, and any game they're involved in shouldn't have a total in the low 40s. Unfortunately, the Chargers' offense is bad, but I continue to believe that Mike McDaniel's system is going to eventually click, and they're going to have some strong offensive outputs sooner rather than later. Now that they face an average Chiefs defense facing an 0-6 record to start the season, now could be the time that their offense comes out firing. While I don’t mind the OVER play, I think this is going to be a lopsided game, especially since Los Angeles is banged up across the board on offense. Ladd McConkey, Quentin Johnston and Tre Harris have all been hurt in 2026, and the Chargers have tackle Rashawn Slater on injured reserve. That’s led to a terrible offense, as L.A. ranks 32nd in the NFL in EPA/Play and 28th in success rate through five weeks. As MacMillan mentioned, this Chiefs offense has been one of the best in the league, and I expect Patrick Mahomes and Co. to take care of business out of a bye week against a Chargers team that has a very slim chance of turning this season around. L.A. has yet to cover the spread in a game this season, and bettors should expect that to change on Sunday. Kenneth Walker III rushes for 200 yards and three touchdowns Jay Biggerstaff-Imagn Images Walker has already accumulated 537 rushing yards and four touchdowns on 87 carries through four games. Those advantages can sustain drives and produce the repeated rushing opportunities necessary for a monster individual afternoon. The prediction goes beyond another efficient outing. Walker reaches 200 rushing yards for the game and scores three times, becoming the central reason Kansas City controls possession and repeatedly finishes drives. There is an important limitation: Los Angeles allows only 5.0 yards per play, the same figure as Kansas City. This is not a forecast built on pretending the Chargers cannot defend. It depends on Walker maintaining his explosiveness while the Chiefs create an unusually favorable game script. If Kansas City builds an early advantage, sustained rushing volume can turn Walker's strong start into the biggest performance of his season. The Chargers intercept Patrick Mahomes twice, including a pick-six Mahomes has thrown nine touchdown passes against two interceptions through four games, with a 106.2 passer rating. Predicting two interceptions in one afternoon means Los Angeles matches his entire season total, despite entering winless. The statistical route to that surprise exists. The Chargers allow opponents to convert just 31.25% of third downs, compared with Kansas City's 37.04%. Forcing longer, obvious passing situations could provide opportunities that disappear when Walker keeps the offense ahead of schedule. Los Angeles needs more than ordinary defensive stops because its offense averages just 16.8 points per game. A defensive touchdown would change both field position and scoreboard pressure without requiring Justin Herbert to repeatedly rescue stalled possessions. The call is that one aggressive coverage read becomes an interception return for a touchdown, while another takeaway interrupts a promising Chiefs drive. That would be an unexpected blemish on Mahomes' efficient opening month. It would also illustrate why a team's record does not eliminate its capacity to produce a game-changing individual moment. Justin Herbert leads a 17-point fourth quarter, but Kansas City survives Herbert's current numbers make this the most counterintuitive offensive prediction: 937 passing yards, five touchdowns, seven interceptions and a 70.2 passer rating through five games. He has also absorbed 17 sacks. Against Denver, he managed 121 passing yards and was sacked five times. Receiving availability remains uncertain after Ladd McConkey dressed without playing, Quentin Johnston missed the game and Tre' Harris suffered a hamstring injury. Nevertheless, the prediction is that Herbert finally finds rhythm against a defense protecting a substantial lead. Two touchdown drives and a field goal produce 17 fourth-quarter points, forcing Kansas City to finish the game with its offense rather than coast. Walker provides that answer. The final forecast is Chiefs 38, Chargers 31: Kansas City remains unbeaten, but Los Angeles delivers a much stronger response than its record suggests. away.blurb: The Kansas City Chiefs officially elevated players from the practice squad ahead of Week 6 against the Los Angeles Chargers. The Chiefs had one specific need this week from their practice squad elevations. Tyquan Thornton is on IR , and Rashee Rice is ruled out for Week 6 . That left only four wide receivers available on the 53-man roster: Xavier Worthy, Jalen Royals, Cyrus Allen, and Nikko Remigio. Naturally, the team's practice squad elevations focused on reinforcing depth at wide receiver. The team elevated WRs Andrew Armstrong and Justin Watson from the practice squad to the 53-man roster for the Week 6 AFC West showdown. Here’s a quick reminder of the league’s practice squad elevation rules. Kansas City Chiefs' Week 6 practice squad elevations give them the wide reinforcements they need vs. Los Angeles Chargers Skip to content College Football Close Menu All College Football The Kansas City Chiefs have elevated WR Andrew Armstrong & WR Justin Watson for Week 6 against the Los Angeles Chargers. NFL clubs can elevate up to two players per week without signing them to the 53-man roster. This temporarily expands 53-man rosters to up to 55 players, but it does not expand game-day roster limits (48). Players can only receive 3 standard elevations per season. Following the game, players automatically revert to the practice squad. Practice squad elevations reset for the postseason. Kansas City Chiefs elevate Andrew Armstrong and Justin Watson from the practice squad As I expected , the Chiefs elevated WR Andrew Armstrong from the practice squad for Week 6. While Omari Evans might seem like a better fit for Tyquan Thornton's role, Armstrong made a strong case for the 53-man roster during training camp and the preseason. He led the team in the preseason with 7 receptions for 85 yards. The 6-foot-4 and 210-pound wideout immediately improves the team's perimeter blocking and gives Patrick Mahomes a big red-zone target. The Chiefs elevated Justin Watson from the practice squad just one week after the veteran returned to Kansas City. He previously played the Tyquan Thornton role , recording 64 receptions for 1,064 yards and 7 touchdowns from 2022-2024. He's coming off an Achilles injury; however, he was a verifiable deep threat in Kansas City, averaging 16.6 yards per reception in his three prior seasons with the team. These two players will likely bolster the trio of Xavier Worthy, Jalen Royals, and Cyrus Allen, who are expected to start at wide receiver on Sunday. home.blurb: The Kansas City Chiefs officially elevated players from the practice squad ahead of Week 6 against the Los Angeles Chargers. The Chiefs had one specific need this week from their practice squad elevations. Tyquan Thornton is on IR , and Rashee Rice is ruled out for Week 6 . That left only four wide receivers available on the 53-man roster: Xavier Worthy, Jalen Royals, Cyrus Allen, and Nikko Remigio. Naturally, the team's practice squad elevations focused on reinforcing depth at wide receiver. The team elevated WRs Andrew Armstrong and Justin Watson from the practice squad to the 53-man roster for the Week 6 AFC West showdown. Here’s a quick reminder of the league’s practice squad elevation rules. Kansas City Chiefs' Week 6 practice squad elevations give them the wide reinforcements they need vs. Los Angeles Chargers Skip to content College Football Close Menu All College Football The Kansas City Chiefs have elevated WR Andrew Armstrong & WR Justin Watson for Week 6 against the Los Angeles Chargers. NFL clubs can elevate up to two players per week without signing them to the 53-man roster. This temporarily expands 53-man rosters to up to 55 players, but it does not expand game-day roster limits (48). Players can only receive 3 standard elevations per season. Following the game, players automatically revert to the practice squad. Practice squad elevations reset for the postseason. Kansas City Chiefs elevate Andrew Armstrong and Justin Watson from the practice squad As I expected , the Chiefs elevated WR Andrew Armstrong from the practice squad for Week 6. While Omari Evans might seem like a better fit for Tyquan Thornton's role, Armstrong made a strong case for the 53-man roster during training camp and the preseason. He led the team in the preseason with 7 receptions for 85 yards. The 6-foot-4 and 210-pound wideout immediately improves the team's perimeter blocking and gives Patrick Mahomes a big red-zone target. The Chiefs elevated Justin Watson from the practice squad just one week after the veteran returned to Kansas City. He previously played the Tyquan Thornton role , recording 64 receptions for 1,064 yards and 7 touchdowns from 2022-2024. He's coming off an Achilles injury; however, he was a verifiable deep threat in Kansas City, averaging 16.6 yards per reception in his three prior seasons with the team. These two players will likely bolster the trio of Xavier Worthy, Jalen Royals, and Cyrus Allen, who are expected to start at wide receiver on Sunday. home.blurb: Unfortunately for quarterback Patrick Mahomes, Rice did not make enough progress to even be considered a game-time decision. He missed all three practices this week and has been ruled out. He will have a chance to return next week though as the injury is not considered serious. The Kansas City Chiefs are coming off their bye week and set to host the Los Angeles Chargers at Arrowhead Stadium in Week 6. The bye week came at a good time for the Chiefs, who suffered multiple wide receiver injury setbacks during their Week 4 win against the Las Vegas Raiders. That includes both Rashee Rice and Tyquan Thornton. Thornton had the worse timeline of the two, dislocating his left ankle and being placed on injured reserve. As for Rice, he suffered a left hamstring non-contact injury in the first quarter, which was concerning. He did have nearly two weeks to try and recover heading into Sunday. In the short term, the Chiefs needed answers and have decided to elevate two wide receivers for their matchup against the Chargers. The team elevated both Andrew Armstrong and Justin Watson onto the active roster, per Matt Derrick of Chiefs Digest. For Watson, this represents his second stint in Kansas City. He was signed just days ago, but given his familiarity with the system and playing for head coach Andy Reid, he is ready in time. As for Armstrong, he has been with the organization since January, was cut during final roster cuts but cleared waivers and has been on the practice squad ever since. Now he will get a chance to make his NFL debut if he checks in on Sunday. Related: Chiefs’ Andy Reid Announces WR Move After Tyreek Hill News

However, the Raiders have surprised everyone and started the season 3-0. Their hot start has cooled down a bit, thanks to facing some heavy hitters in the conference. They lost their last two games, first falling to the Kansas City Chiefs ,30-27, in a hard-fought AFC West battle. Last week, they struggled against the defending AFC Champion New England Patriots , losing 45-17 and showing cracks in their unlikely season. The Bills can relate to Vegas' last loss, because Buffalo's only defeat this season came against their AFC East rival. Buffalo lost to the Patriots 29-26 in Week 4. Last week, the Bills squeaked out a win against the Los Angeles Rams in overtime, with a blocked kick saving the game for Buffalo. Bills vs. Raiders: need to know Ball security: The Bills do well in many categories, but turnovers have been an issue lately. Bills have nine turnovers in the last three games, with four coming from Josh Allen . Last week, running back James Cook had a crucial turnover in overtime, and while it worked out in the end, it did add to the turnover problem building on Buffalo's offense. The Las Vegas Raiders received encouraging news regarding Ashton Jeanty's health as the team prepares for Sunday's matchup against the Buffalo Bills. After spending much of the season dealing with foot and ankle injuries, the second-year running back appears to be making significant progress. Speaking with reporters at his locker Thursday, Jeanty said he was feeling great and that this was the best he had felt all season, according to ESPN reporter Ryan McFadden. "He's playing," Kubiak said when asked about potentially sitting Jeanty. Kubiak also noted that Jeanty was making progress in his recovery, raising the possibility that he could take on a larger workload during practice. Jeanty's comments Thursday offered further encouragement, suggesting that the running back is beginning to feel more comfortable after battling injuries throughout the season. The former Boise State standout first suffered an ankle injury during training camp in August. While he recovered in time for the regular season, the issue has continued to linger, making it difficult for him to play at full strength. Jeanty appeared to aggravate the ankle during Las Vegas' Week 4 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs before dealing with an additional foot issue ahead of last Sunday's matchup against the New England Patriots.

away.blurb: Starting right tackle Spencer Brown left Monday night's 37-34 victory over the Los Angeles Rams because of a back injury and did not return, adding another starter to Buffalo's list of health concerns. NFL teams have to submit a report on practice participation on Wednesday, Thursday and Friday for a Sunday game. There are three levels of practice participation that can be designated: did not participate, limited participation and full participation. Bills athletic trainers tended to Brown on the field before he walked off under his own power. He appeared to grab at his back while walking toward the sideline and went directly into the blue medical tent. Brown later went to the locker room and did not return. Buffalo initially listed Brown as questionable before downgrading him to out during the fourth quarter. He was listed as questionable but did not play Monday. Oliver did not practice at all last week. Joshua Palmer was ruled out against the Rams after suffering a shoulder injury during Friday's practice. Palmer was not listed on Thursday's injury report before being limited Friday and sitting out Saturday. He was listed as questionable but was inactive against the Rams. Zane Durant is eligible to return after beginning the season on injured reserve. Buffalo can designate Durant to return and open his 21-day practice window when he is medically cleared. Tyrell Shavers is eligible to return after beginning the season on the physically unable to perform list. The Bills can designate him to return and open his 21-day practice window when he is ready. Ashton Jeanty played against New England despite being listed as questionable because of ankle and foot injuries. "Unless I can't run, jump, I'm playing. Football is a tough game. You're never gonna play feeling 100 percent," Jeanty said. "So at the end of the day, I just want to go out there and do my best for my teammates and whatever it takes." He was ruled out for the remainder of the game. Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said Monday that Nailor is expected to return to practice this week as he works through the NFL concussion protocol. home.blurb: Starting right tackle Spencer Brown left Monday night's 37-34 victory over the Los Angeles Rams because of a back injury and did not return, adding another starter to Buffalo's list of health concerns. NFL teams have to submit a report on practice participation on Wednesday, Thursday and Friday for a Sunday game. There are three levels of practice participation that can be designated: did not participate, limited participation and full participation. Bills athletic trainers tended to Brown on the field before he walked off under his own power. He appeared to grab at his back while walking toward the sideline and went directly into the blue medical tent. Brown later went to the locker room and did not return. Buffalo initially listed Brown as questionable before downgrading him to out during the fourth quarter. He was listed as questionable but did not play Monday. Oliver did not practice at all last week. Joshua Palmer was ruled out against the Rams after suffering a shoulder injury during Friday's practice. Palmer was not listed on Thursday's injury report before being limited Friday and sitting out Saturday. He was listed as questionable but was inactive against the Rams. Zane Durant is eligible to return after beginning the season on injured reserve. Buffalo can designate Durant to return and open his 21-day practice window when he is medically cleared. Tyrell Shavers is eligible to return after beginning the season on the physically unable to perform list. The Bills can designate him to return and open his 21-day practice window when he is ready. Ashton Jeanty played against New England despite being listed as questionable because of ankle and foot injuries. "Unless I can't run, jump, I'm playing. Football is a tough game. You're never gonna play feeling 100 percent," Jeanty said. "So at the end of the day, I just want to go out there and do my best for my teammates and whatever it takes." He was ruled out for the remainder of the game. Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said Monday that Nailor is expected to return to practice this week as he works through the NFL concussion protocol. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights The last time these two teams met in Week 4 of the 2025 season, they combined for the highest-scoring tie in the Super Bowl era Getty Images One of the NFL's highest-scoring rivalries will be renewed on "Sunday Night Football" in Week 6 when the Green Bay Packers (3-2) host the Dallas Cowboys (2-3) at Lambeau Field on Sunday night. Last season, the Packers traveled down to Texas to face the Cowboys at AT&T Stadium, and the two teams tied at 40-40, the highest-scoring tie in the Super Bowl era, since 1996, per CBS Sports Research. The game featured seven lead changes, including six consecutive touchdown drives with a lead change in the second half. However, this rivalry hasn't exactly been very competitive in terms of the games' final outcomes, with the Cowboys seeking their first win against the Packers since the 2016 regular season, quarterback Dak Prescott's rookie year. Since that game, Dallas is 0-5-1 in the last six games against Green Bay despite scoring 31 points per game in that stretch. The problem is their defense has allowed a combined 37 points per game during the six-game winless streak against the Packers. That's the most points per game scored by a team's offense during a six-game winless span against an opponent in NFL history, per CBS Sports Research. Sunday will mark Packers quarterback Jordan Love's first home start against the Cowboys, with both of his games against Dallas coming on the road -- a 48-32 wild card round win in the 2023 season and the 40-40 tie last year. It will also mark a homecoming for two former Packers who are now Cowboys: three-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle Kenny Clark and Pro Bowl edge rusher Rashan Gary . Let's dig into this primetime fight against two of the NFL's most historic franchises, but first, here's how you can watch: Where to watch Cowboys vs. Packers Date: Sunday, Oct. 18 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: Lambeau Field (Green Bay, Wisconsin) TV: NBC | Stream: Fubo (try for free) Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Packers -1.5, O/U 53.5 (via DraftKings Sportsbook) Cowboys vs. Packers need to know Cowboys looking to fix bad vibes on defense: In Week 5, Dallas lost a home game 24-16 on "Thursday Night Football" to the previously 0-4 Tampa Bay Buccaneers , a team it was favored by 9.5 points. Tampa Bay was starting undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels , making his second career start in place of an injured Baker Mayfield , and Dallas allowed the Buccaneers to control the game with 241 rushing yards. That was the most for the Buccaneers in a game since the 2024 season. This week, there has been speculation from owner and general manager Jerry Jones about first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker moving upstairs to the booth, but Parker and head coach Brian Schottenheimer maintained he will remain on the sideline. Dallas' performance improvement plan has begun with the hiring of former Cleveland Browns coach Mike Pettine as a senior assistant . Pettine actually gave Parker his first job in the NFL when he was Green Bay's defensive coordinator in 2019. Dallas knows that being the league's 31st-ranked defense (395.4 total yards allowed per game), last-place run defense (168.4 rushing yards allowed per game), and worst third-down defense (52.6% third-down conversion rate allowed) won't cut it. How fixable are the issues? "Very fixable because they're under our control," Parker said. "Very fixable." Cowboys All-Pro defensive tackle Quinnen Williams agrees. "Just from the aspect of the things that we can control are the things that we're messing up on. Effort. Playing with our technique. Playing better, things like that. Those are things we can control as a unit, we can control as a unit. It's fixable. We just have to make our best effort to fix those things. Packers' Jordan Love aims to maintain an explosive passing game to Christian Watson and Matthew Golden : Packers quarterback Jordan Love is fresh off his best game of 2026 in Week 5, a 31-7 beatdown of the Chicago Bears at Lambeau Field. Love completed 25 of his 31 throws for 367 yards and 2 touchdowns against Chicago, which makes him the Packers' record holder for the most passing yards in a game against the Bears at Lambeau Field. He beat the previous record of 345 yards passing by Lynn Dickey, set back in 1983. The victory, 24 points, ranks as the largest win against the Bears since 2014, the year Rodgers won the second of his four NFL MVPs. The Packers are now 5-3 against the Bears in Love's eight career starts against them since 2023, including playoffs. "We were flowing today. Executed at a really high level. I was proud of everybody. That's what it looks like when we play to our standard, and we got playmakers making plays down the field, O-line doing a great job," Love said postgame on FOX . "That's the standard for us. ... This is huge. This is a win we needed at home, getting us rolling and keep building off this." Love went big-game hunting with regularity to both wide receiver Christian Watson (143 yards receiving and 2 receiving touchdowns on 6 catches) and wide receiver Matthew Golden (123 yards receiving on 6 catches), making Watson and Golden the first Green Bay duo with 120-plus yards receiving in a game since 2016. It last occurred when Davante Adams and Jordy Nelson accomplished the feat against the Tennessee Titans 10 years ago. Love hit Watson for gains of 42 yards (the game's first touchdown that made the score 7-0), 31 yards and 53 yards (Love's second touchdown pass that made the score 20-7 with 13:10 left in the third quarter). He connected with Golden on throws of 36 yards and 50 yards. In total, Love connected on six of eight of his eight throws of 20-plus air yards for a career-high 258 yards and 2 touchdowns on his passes of 20-plus air yards. Per the league's Next Gen stats , only Russell Wilson (264 with the New York Giants in Week 2 of the 2025 season against the Dallas Cowboys ) had more in the NGS era (since 2016). According to ESPN Insights , Love joined Ben Roethlisberger as the only players with five completions of 30-plus air yards in a game since ESPN began tracking the metric 20 years ago in 2006. Slowing this high-flying passing attack down will be a tall task for a struggling Cowboys defense. A stoppable force vs. a movable object: The Packers rank dead last in the NFL in rushing yards per game (60.4) and third-down offense (27.6% conversion rate) thanks to missing running back Josh Jacobs while he was on the commissioner's exempt list and dealing with some offensive line injuries. Across from them on the line of scrimmage at Lambeau Field on Sunday will be the Cowboys' last-ranked run defense (168.4 rushing yards per game allowed) and last-ranked third-down defense (52.6% conversion rate allowed). Whichever team can find an edge here will likely emerge victorious. New Cowboys CB Joey Porter Jr . primed to return in primetime: New Dallas Cowboys cornerback Joey Porter Jr. was set to play his first full game as a Cowboy in Week 5 before a stomach bug made him a late scratch hours before kickoff. However, Porter Jr. is now recovered from his illness and aims to play a full starter's load of snaps. He played on 48.1% (25 of 52) of the Cowboys' defensive snaps in their 34-30 road win over the Houston Texans in Week 4 just days after being acquired in a trade from the Pittsburgh Steelers earlier that week. He is officially listed as questionable to play on Sunday with an ankle injury, but on Wednesday he said he is "definitely" ready to be a full-time starter for Dallas. Parker agreed, saying the team is ready for him to have a "heavily increased" workload against the Packers. Cowboys vs. Packers prediction Despite Porter Jr. likely returning to action for Dallas in Week 6, their defense won't be able to stifle Love, Watson and Golden through the air. Whichever receiver between Watson and Golden that cornerback DaRon Bland , who has struggled with his footing on the field of late, will break free for big gains on a consistent basis. Yes, the Cowboys do have the NFL's No. 7 scoring offense (27.6 points per game) powered by Prescott, wide receiver CeeDee Lamb , wide receiver George Pickens and running back Javonte Williams . However, Dallas' defense struggles will limit their offense's ability to find a rhythm. The Cowboys are averaging 3.07 points per drive, the second-highest by a team under .500 through five games this century per CBS Sports Research, but their 45 drives this season are the second fewest in the league this season. Among the NFL teams that have played in all five weeks of the 2026 season, Dallas' 45 drives stand as the fewest. Can you believe it? This weekend, two AFC South rivals in the Houston Texans and Jacksonville Jaguars will battle in London, while Caleb Williams looks to return to the lineup against the Atlanta Falcons after missing the last three games. We also have an intriguing matchup in the NFC on Sunday night between the Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers , while the Washington Commanders will look to get back on track against the 49ers in San Francisco following their embarrassing tie with the New York Giants . Dan Quinn needs to find a way to get his team to refocus after they completely forgot about the clock in overtime. Which teams should you pick in Week 6, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 13 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Houston Texans vs. Jacksonville Jaguars (-3) (London) Dajani (Texans +3): The Jaguars have established themselves as one of the best teams in the AFC. While that's objectively true, they certainly aren't perfect. They probably should have dominated a short-handed Philadelphia Eagles team last week, yet didn't. Additionally, there are some questions about the offensive operation. Jacksonville went 0-3 in the red zone last week, including two trips where the Jags failed to score any points from the one-yard line. As for the Texans, they are coming off their first win of the season against the lowly Tennessee Titans . I predict they keep that momentum going and score an upset victory across the pond. DeMeco Ryans is calling defensive plays again, and C.J. Stroud is actually playing good football. He's tied for the most 20-yard completions (21) in the NFL this season. Houston is also 14-2 SU and 11-4-1 ATS in its last 16 divisional games away from home. … Prediction: Texans 21, Jaguars 18 Dubin (Jaguars -3): I think it's a real advantage that the Jaguars have already been in London for a week while the Texans haven't yet traveled across the pond. Jacksonville, as Dajani mentioned, has established itself as one of the best teams in the AFC. The offense has been efficient and explosive, and the defense has looked good as well. I know the Jags struggled with the Eagles for a bit of last week's game and probably should have lost, but Houston has only beaten a Tennessee team that is barely functional. It's not like the Texans have looked good at any point. Their defense has disappointed, and they can't run the ball whatsoever. … Prediction: Jaguars 24, Texans 20 Chicago Bears (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Falcons +3): It looks like Caleb Williams is going to return to the lineup after missing three games with his hamstring injury, and it also looks like Michael Penix Jr . will play after missing the very end of "Sunday Night Football" with his rib injury. The Chicago Bears have racked up their most rushing yards per contest (173.2) through five games since 1988, but keep an eye on the status of Kyle Monangai , who missed Week 5 with a toe injury. Last week's loss to the Packers was concerning from a defensive standpoint. The Bears have actually allowed 30 points over three straight road games (dating back to last year), which is tied for the longest streak in TEAM HISTORY. I'm going to take the points with the home team, and take Bijan Robinson and Co. to bounce back. … Prediction: Falcons 30, Bears 27 Dubin (Bears -3): The impending return of Caleb Williams has me leaning toward Chicago here. In the one non-monsoon game that Williams played, the Bears dropped 59 points on the Panthers . They ran the ball at will and created explosive plays in the passing game. Their defense was exposed a bit by the Packers last week, and the Falcons could get going offensively here ... if Michael Penix Jr. actually plays through the rib injury he suffered last week. At least some of this pick is thinking Tua Tagovailoa could start under center for Atlanta. … Prediction: Bears 23, Falcons 17 Baltimore Ravens (-4.5) at Cleveland Browns Dajani ( Ravens -4.5): I'm not going to bash the Cleveland Browns for their loss to the New York Jets in that gross weather, where punter Corey Bojorquez missed a snap and granted the Jets 34 yards of field position to set up the game-winning touchdown. But I am nervous about Cleveland's injuries with guys like Carson Schwesinger , Mason Graham , Mike Hall Jr., Tytus Howard , Quinshon Judkins and KC Concepcion banged up. I think it's fair to say that Lamar Jackson is expected back this week after sitting one game with his ankle injury, but I was wildly impressed with this Ravens defense and their ability to shut down what was statistically the hottest offense in the NFL since Michael Penix Jr. returned. Bijan Robinson rushed for 86 yards on Sunday night. He was averaging about 170 rushing yards per game with Penix under center. If it weren't for all the walking wounded in Cleveland, I would probably side with the home dogs. Not this time. … Prediction: Ravens 26, Browns 20 Dubin (Ravens -4.5): I can't tell if this line is assuming the return of Lamar Jackson or not, but r ecent reporting suggests he has a chance to return to action . If he does, I think the Ravens win this game by a lot. The Browns might be 3-2, but they have not played like an above .500 team so far. Each of their wins required a game-winning drive late in the fourth quarter, and that's not at all sustainable. I don't trust that their offense can get anything going given the various injuries to the skill-position players, and if Jackson is back, I don't think the Ravens' offense can be stopped. … Prediction: Ravens 31, Browns 14 Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles (-1.5) Dajani (Panthers +1.5): CBS Sports legend John Breech pointed out that the Eagles are facing a scheduling disadvantage this week that no team has ever been able to overcome. Philly is, of course, coming off an international game and facing a team that is coming off its bye. This has only happened four times, but the team coming off the international game is 0-4 SU and 0-3-1 ATS. That's pretty fascinating. The Eagles have covered the spread just once all season, while the last time the Panthers were on the field, they registered an impressive victory against the Detroit Lions . Bryce Young threw for 329 yards and two touchdowns, Chuba Hubbard rushed for 122 yards and two touchdowns and Tet McMillan caught 14 passes for 192 yards and -- you guessed it -- two touchdowns. I have some legitimate concerns about the Panthers defense, but I'll take the upset in Philly. … Prediction: Panthers 23, Eagles 21 Dubin (Eagles -1.5): I don't feel good about this one at all. I'm basically just throwing my hands in the air and saying, well, the Eagles can't lose again , can they? … Prediction: Eagles 20, Panthers 17 Dallas Cowboys at Green Bay Packers (-1.5) (SNF) Dajani (Packers -1.5): I told you the Packers were going to upset the Bears last week, and that something "weird" was going to happen. The "weird" came in the form of a 31-7 beatdown of Tyson Bagent . It's tough to trust Dallas after watching an undrafted rookie quarterback making his second career start come into AT&T Stadium and drop 419 yards of total offense on the Cowboys' head in prime time. Now, they have to go to Lambeau Field and try to stop a quarterback in Jordan Love , who is clearly finding his rhythm, having just thrown for 367 yards and two touchdowns. CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens are definitely a fun duo, but so are Christian Watson and Matthew Golden . Heck, let's make it a trio with tight end Tucker Kraft . … Prediction: Packers 27, Cowboys 24 Dubin (Packers -1.5): The Dallas defense is just too bad for me to feel comfortable picking the Cowboys against a team that has an offensive pulse. The Packers showed last week that they are capable of throwing the ball all over the yard even if their running game can't get going. Even with the return of Joey Porter Jr. , I expect that Green Bay will get one or all of Christian Watson, Matthew Golden and Tucker Kraft going down the field. Dallas should put up points, too, because the Packers' defense is no great shakes, but I'm taking Green Bay to win here. … Prediction: Packers 33, Cowboys 28 Washington Commanders at San Francisco 49ers (-7.5) (MNF) Dajani (49ers -7.5): I am genuinely curious how the Commanders running the clock out on themselves affected the locker room.
