Stroud, Green Bay gets its ground game rolling against Dallas, and Justin Herbert breaks out of an ugly slump Getty Images Anything can happen in the NFL , and the start to Week 6 of the 2026 season certainly hammered home that fact. In the Denver Broncos (4-2) 17-14 "Thursday Night Football" overtime win over the Seattle Seahawks , they triumphed at home despite averaging 2.9 yards per play. That's the fewest in Sean Payton's 318-game head-coaching career, and Denver's 168 total yards of offense ranked as their fewest in a victory since Pro Football Hall of Fame quarterback John Elway's first start as a rookie in 1983. Quarterback Bo Nix , who ranks dead last in the NFL in yards per pass attempt at 5.6, improved to a 13-3 career record in games when he averages six yards per pass attempt or fewer, the best of all-time minimum 15 starts per CBS Sports Research, after averaging 4.0 yards per pass attempt on Thursday. All other active quarterbacks have a combined .283 winning percentage in starts where they average six yards per pass attempt or fewer. That's absolutely unfathomable. What other hijinks could take place across the rest of the NFL's Week 6 slate? Here is a look at five bold predictions. Packers run for over 100 yards for first time in 2026 vs. Cowboys The Green Bay Packers are back above .500 after quarterback Jordan Love's laser show (367 yards and 2 passing touchdowns while completing 25 of his 31 throws) in a 31-7 beatdown of the Chicago Bears at Lambeau Field in Week 5. Now that they have a winning record, they're now the owners of the third-fewest rushing yards per game (60.4) by any team above .500 through five games of a season in league history, per CBS Sports Research. Green Bay's NFL-worst rushing offense also ranks as the fewest rushing yards per game through games of any season in the Packers' 106-season franchise history. Some of that has to do with the absence of running back Josh Jacobs , who is on the commissioner's exempt list after being charged with two misdemeanors, and some of that has to do with the team's beat-up offensive line. However, the offensive line has stabilized with veterans Laken Tomlinson and Travis Glover stabilizing the team's guard play. That's one of the reasons why the Packers will run for over 100 yards as a team for the first time in 2026 against the Dallas Cowboys on "Sunday Night Football." The others are that Green Bay running back MarShawn Lloyd is a freight train at 5 feet 9 inches tall and 220 pounds, and the Cowboys have the league's worst run defense (168.4 rushing yards allowed per game). Dallas allowed the Tampa Bay Buccaneers to go off for 241 yards rushing, their most in a game since 2024, on "Thursday Night Football" in Week 5. Facing a leaky defense like that and Lloyd fresh off running through Bears cornerback Jaylon Johnson's face for a touchdown in Week 5, Lloyd and the Packers cross the century mark on the ground for the first time this season. Marshawn Lloyd trucks a guy on his way to the end zone 😤 @CHIvsGB on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/NNcSwQfTOU Marvin Harrison Jr. has first 100-yard receiving game since his rookie year Houston Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud is quietly playing efficient football: he has the fifth-most passing attempts without an interception (185) through five games in NFL history while throwing for the fourth-most passing yards in the NFL (1,402) this season. The Texans (1-4) have a high-volume passing offense this season because of their struggling rushing offense, and that will lead to Houston's newest player, 2024 fourth overall pick wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. , thriving in his team debut against the AFC South-leading Jacksonville Jaguars (4-1). How much will he soar in his first game back with his former Ohio State Buckeyes teammate in Stroud? Harrison Jr. will produce his first 100-yard receiving game since his rookie year in 2024 and just the third overall 100-yard receiving game of his young career on Sunday. He and Stroud were Ohio State teammates for two seasons from 2021 to 2022, and Harrison Jr.'s 14 receiving touchdowns when Stroud was the starting quarterback in 2022 are tied for the third most in a single season in Buckeyes' history. Harrison Jr. also set or tied career-highs in catches (77), receiving yards (1,263) and receiving touchdowns (14) in that 2022 season with Stroud. Houston will be celebrating their newest trade acquisition's 100-yard game when the clock hits zero at Wembley Stadium on Sunday. Justin Herbert ends fourth-quarter turnover streak and multi-passing touchdown drought vs. Chiefs The Los Angeles Chargers are injury-plagued and riding the struggle bus at 0-5 to start 2026. Pro Bowl quarterback Justin Herbert is tied for the most interceptions (seven) and turnovers (nine) in the NFL this season, and he has a couple of ugly streaks going against him. He has five consecutive games with a fourth-quarter turnover, making him the first quarterback since Charlie Frye in 2006 to do that. Herbert also hasn't thrown for multiple passing touchdowns in a game in his last seven games, the longest such streak of his career. However, he will play a clean fourth quarter and throw multiple touchdown passes against the 4-0 Kansas City Chiefs at Arrowhead on Sunday. The last time the Chiefs were on the field in Week 4, 38-year-old Kirk Cousins threw for 365 yards, 2 touchdowns and an interception on 31 of 52 passes in a narrow 30-27 Chiefs win. Herbert will snap out of his funk and raise his level to go toe-to-toe with Mahomes by having a clean fourth quarter and throwing multiple touchdowns for the first time in a while. Jets' Geno Smith throws first interception of 2026 at Patriots Geno Smith is on an incredible public relations campaign in 2026 with the New York Jets . After leading the NFL with 17 interceptions as a Las Vegas Raider in 2025, he hasn't thrown any through five games this season. Smith has six passing touchdowns to no interceptions this season, a stark contrast from his touchdown-to-interception ratio at this time a year ago when he had the same number of touchdown passes (six) but with nine interceptions. He is only the second quarterback in NFL history with no interceptions through five starts, after leading the league in interceptions the previous season, and is tied with Vinny Testaverde, also with the Jets, back in 2001, per CBS Sports Research. However, Smith will throw his first interception of the season in Week 6 at the New England Patriots . Patriots All-Pro cornerback Christian Gonzalez (shoulder) is on track to return this week, fully practicing on Thursday after being limited on Wednesday. In his first game back after a two-game absence, Gonzalez will intercept Smith for the veteran's first interception of 2026. Saints won't cover as road favorite at Giants Yes, your eyes don't deceive you. According to DraftKings Sportsbook , the 1-4 New Orleans Saints are favored by 1.5 points over the 3-1-1 New York Giants on the road at MetLife Stadium. Perhaps the ugliness of the NFC East leader's 27-27 tie at the Washington Commanders in Week 5 is pushing the spread in favor of the Saints. Maybe it's the allure of New Orleans quarterback Tyler Shough , whose 1,299 passing yards rank as the seventh-most in the NFL. Regardless, that positions the Saints to win on Sunday, as they have covered in seven consecutive road games, the longest active road cover streak in the entire NFL, per CBS Sports Research. However, the Saints' road cover streak will be broken on Sunday because Jameis Winston plays a more efficient brand of football than Shough. Sure, Winston's 57.6% is the second-worst in the NFL among 31 qualified quarterbacks in 2026, but he is starting to turn a corner and find a groove as an NFL starting quarterback once again. He is the first Giants quarterback with three-plus passing touchdowns in consecutive games since Eli Manning in 2016, and Winston didn't throw a single interception after having two in Week 4 against the Arizona Cardinals a couple of weeks ago. On the other hand, Shough has a turnover problem: his eight this season are the third-most in the league. Winston will outduel Shough and prevent a Saints road cover for the eighth consecutive such game. Now Playing Share Share Video Marvin Harrison Jr. breaks out with C.J. The Cowboys fell victim to the trap game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Dallas was heavily favored, and rightly so, as Tampa Bay was 0-4 and starting an undrafted rookie quarterback. But Dallas failed to so much as show up and fell to 2-3 on the year. The Packers, on the other hand, absolutely throttled the Chicago Bears in what was far and away Green Bay's best game on both sides of the ball. Now, all of the talk of the Packers' demise has been shelved. These two teams squared off last season and battled to a 40-40 tie. Before that, Green Bay had beaten Dallas in eight of their last nine meetings. Will the Packers continue their dominance over the Cowboys? Or will Dallas flip the script and pull out a win? Here's what experts from different media outlets think. Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Packers: 26 The biggest problem for the Cowboys in this game is Green Bay's ability to move the ball through the air . The Packers had struggled offensively over the first four contests, but they found their rhythm in Week 5 by torching the Bears with the deep ball. Defending the pass has been a major issue for the Cowboys this season, with Dallas ranking 21st. That doesn't even do justice for how bad it has really been. The Cowboys' ranking would be even worse if teams weren't abusing Christian Parker's unit on the ground. The good news for the Cowboys is the Packers haven't been able to run the football with any semblance of success, although Dallas presents a perfect get-right opportunity with their league-worst showing against the run this season. Green Bay has also struggled to stop the run, ranking 24th, but the Cowboys aren't running the ball like they did last season and it remains to be seen if they can capitalize on Green Bay's woes. Another problem for the Cowboys is the Packers are giving up the fifth-fewest yards per game through the air and if that holds true this week and the run game doesn't get on track, it's going to be tough sledding for Dallas' offense. Joey Porter Jr.'s return is going to make a dent in Dallas' passing game struggles, but the Cowboys still have the other side of the field to defend and DaRon Bland has proven incapable of doing that. The slot is a another concern if Caleb Downs is still playing most or all of his snaps at safety like he has amid the Cowboys' slew of injuries at safety. The Cowboys will get their points to keep this game close, but we're highly skeptical Dallas' secondary and pass-rush will do enough to keep Green Bay's passing attack at bay enough to emerge victorious. away.headline: Packers elevate 2 players from practice squad for Week 6 vs. Cowboys
away.blurb: The Green Bay Packers elevated edge rusher Arron Mosby and wide receiver Coleman Owen from the practice squad to the gameday roster for Week 6 of the 2026 season. Both Mosby and Owen will be available for Matt LaFleur's team against the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday night. Mosby gives the Packers fifth available edge rusher, potentially allowing a player like Lukas Van Ness to play more snaps on the interior -- where the defense is dealing with injuries to Javon Hargrave, Warren Brinson and Jonathan Ford, who are all now on injured reserve. Hargrave and Ford were placed on injured reserve on Saturday, and the Packers currently have only four active defensive linemen: Devonte Wyatt, Karl Brooks, Chris McClellan and Anthony Campbell. It could get shaky very fast up front against the Cowboys if the Packers suffer another injury. Owen is up to the gameday roster despite signing in Green Bay only 17 days ago. He is a slot receiver, and the Packers are lacking in depth there with Moore and Jayden Reed on injured reserve. More than likely, Owen will be in the running to return punts and kicks, two roles he's handled at the NFL level previously (played in two games with the Indianapolis Colts in 2025, returning one punt and five kickoffs). The Packers did not elevate cornerback Domani Jackson or Elijah Culp, suggesting the team thinks Brandon Cisse (questionable, hip) will play Sunday against the Cowboys. The team is still shorthanded at the position without backup Benjamin St-Juste, who is out with a hamstring injury. Neither elevation helps solve the apparent injury situations along the defensive line or at cornerback, but as is the case with most elevations from the practice squad, both are likely special teams related. Mosby was a core special teamer for the Packers in 2024 and 2025, and Owen provides an additional option at both kick and punt returner with Skyy Moore now on injured reserve. This is the first time the Packers have used a practice squad elevation since Week 1. Before the regular season opener, the Packers elevated Bo Melton and Kristian Welch, who are now both on the 53-man roster. Teams can elevate up to two players from the practice squad each week. Players can be elevated three times, so Mosby and Owen are both down to two elevations remaining for the 2026 season. Practice squad elevations by week Week 1: WR Bo Melton, LB Kristian Welch Week 6: EDGE Arron Mosby, WR Coleman Owen This article originally appeared on Packers Wire: Packers elevate 2 players from practice squad for Week 6 vs. Cowboys

away.headline: Green Bay Packers offense could be in for a big day against woeful and injured Dallas Cowboys defense in Week 6
away.blurb: The biggest challenge Green Bay will face this weekend is on defense. Dallas, of course, boasts a stellar wide receiver duo in George Pickens and CeeDee Lamb and have a Pro Bowl-caliber quarterback in Dak Prescott. What is more, the Packers secondary is banged up with Brandon Cisse listed as questionable due to a hip injury suffered in practice. Specifically, this could be a game that sees the Packers’ run game get back on track. Green Bay ranks last in the NFL with 60.4 rushing yards per game. And while Josh Jacobs will return in Week Seven, that does not help them now in Week Six. Dallas’ defense, however, ranks last in the NFL in rushing yards allowed per game with 168.4. This means, of course, that Marshawn Lloyd, Pierre Strong, and Kaleb Johnson will all be competing for future snaps with their opportunities on Sunday night. Jacobs is going to take over as the starting running back when he returns, which means one of the three is going to be out of a job. As such, look for them to have extra motivation as they attempt to make some noise against what has been the league’s worst run defense. The Green Bay Packers are set to take on the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday Night Football this weekend. Now 3-2, Green Bay has won two consecutive games, including a 31-7 demolishing of the hated Chicago Bears in Week Five. Recently, the Packers made some significant changes on their offensive line due to poor play from unit in the first three games of the season. Laken Tomlinson has been a godsend at left guard as Aaron Banks has struggled to get and stay healthy. Travis Glover has been a pleasant surprise at right guard, and Anthony Belton has emerged as one of the best right tackles in the game. Fans may be surprised to learn he has the NFL’s third-longest current streak of snaps played without allowing a pressure. This improved play in the trenches has done wonders for Green Bay’s offense. Sunday night should be another big game for Jordan Love and his fellow playmakers due to the state of Dallas’ defense. The Green Bay Packers offense is facing a woeful Dallas Cowboys defense That does not even take into account how the defensive unit is already going to be without Micah Parsons, Edgerrin Cooper, and Javon Hargrave. This all being said, the Cowboys defense has been downright terrible so far this season. Through the first five games of 2026, they ranked second-to-last in the NFL allowing 395.4 yards per game. Only the Detroit Lions, whom Green Bay faces in Week Seven, are worse. Meanwhile, Jordan Love is coming off of a game that saw him throw for over 360 yards. Matthew Golden and Christian Watson each had over 120 yards receiving last week, and are quickly becoming recognized as one of the NFL’s best wide receiver duos alongside Pickens and Lamb. Sunday night could help them get even more recognition in this area. home.headline: Packers’ Latest Bombshell Micah Parsons Report Is Bad News
home.blurb: NFL insider Tom Pelissero reported Saturday that the earliest realistic return date for Parsons is Nov. 8 against the New England Patriots. That timeline would keep the All-Pro off the field for the first eight games of the 17-game regular season. A Nov. 8 debut would put Parsons right around the halfway point of the schedule. Missing the Patriots game as well would push his absence past half the season, matching earlier projections from June that he could sit out upwards of half the year following ACL surgery. Running back Josh Jacobs, who had also been unavailable, received positive news Friday when the NFL removed him from the commissioner’s exempt list. He is cleared to return to practice and can play when the Packers visit the Detroit Lions on Oct. 25. If Parsons returns for the Patriots, he would be available for later matchups against the Vikings, Buffalo Bills, Los Angeles Rams, Chicago Bears and Houston Texans. Packers' Latest Bombshell Micah Parsons Report Is Bad News NFL AFC North Notre Dame Women's Basketball San Francisco Giants Trade Rumors South Carolina Women's Basketball St. Louis Cardinals Trade Rumors The Green Bay Packers appear increasingly likely to go without star edge rusher Micah Parsons until at least mid-November as he continues recovering from a serious knee injury. “The soonest Parsons appears to have a realistic chance of returning is November 8 against the Patriots,” Pelissero wrote . The Packers have compiled a 3-2 record through five games without Parsons. They sit second in the NFC North behind the undefeated Minnesota Vikings. Green Bay’s defense has recorded 14 sacks in those five contests. Lukas Van Ness leads the team with 2.5 sacks while the unit adjusts to life without its top pass rusher. Parsons tore his ACL and suffered meniscus damage on Dec. 14, 2025, in a loss to the Denver Broncos. He underwent surgery on Dec. 29 and remains on the reserve/physically unable to perform list. He is now roughly 9½ months removed from the procedure. In 14 games last season after arriving via trade, Parsons posted 12.5 sacks, 41 tackles, 27 quarterback hits and two forced fumbles. He earned first-team All-Pro honors and a Pro Bowl selection for the fifth time. The Packers acquired him from the Dallas Cowboys in August 2025, sending defensive tackle Kenny Clark plus first-round picks in 2026 and 2027 in exchange. Green Bay then signed him to a four-year extension worth approximately $188 million. Green Bay faces a challenging stretch before the Nov. 8 window, starting with a Sunday night matchup against the Cowboys. The schedule also includes a trip to Detroit and a Thursday night home game against the Carolina Panthers. His presence has been viewed as a potential difference-maker for a Packers team looking to contend in the second half of the season after a solid start without him. Additionally, All-Pro pass rusher Micah Parsons is getting closer and closer to his own return. NFL insider expects Micah Parsons to return in Week 9 for the Green Bay Packers Initially, many hoped that the All-Pro pass rusher would be able to return for Green Bay’s Week Six matchup against his former team. However, the Packers have not opened up his practice window as they want to ensure that he is 100% healthy and not at risk for any soft tissue injuries because of rushing a return to the field. “A league source tells me Parsons might not return until Week 9, against the Patriots on Nov. 8. The Packers did not open his practice window this week to begin his return. In Week 7, Green Bay plays the Detroit Lions before hosting the Panthers on “’Thursday Night Football’; believing Parsons needs more than a week to ramp up, the short-week turnaround would be difficult to pull off.” If this is truly the targeted return date, it would be realistic to see Parsons designated for return by Green Bay this week. This means he would be able to practice with the rest of the team, and the Packers would have 21 days to add him to the active roster. While he will not play in that many games in 2026, Green Bay is hopeful that his return will take their already impressive defense under Jonathan Gannon to an even higher level. The Green Bay Packers have lost several players to season-ending injuries already this year. These include defensive stars Edgerrin Cooper and Javon Hargrave as well as offensive stars Zach Tom and Jayden Reed. Despite these losses, and terrible play from their offensive line early in year, Green Bay has gone 3-2 in their first five games. Parsons, who was acquired prior to the start of the 2025 season in a trade with the Dallas Cowboys, tore his ACL in late in the year and has missed every game of 2026 thus far. Jonathan Jones of The Athletic reported on Saturday morning that those around the NFL expect Parsons back in Week Nine when Green Bay faces the New England Patriots : Last season, Parsons became the first player in NFL history to record 12+ sacks in each of his first five seasons. He had 12.5 in 14 games played in his first season with the Packers and was named First Team All-Pro. Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs is set to return to the field after missing six games, but the NFL's decision has drawn strong reactions from fans. The league announced that Jacobs will be removed from the Commissioner Exempt List on October 19, making him eligible to play against the Detroit Lions in Week 7. The decision comes after his May arrest and subsequent legal case involving misdemeanor battery and criminal damage to property charges. Jacobs' attorneys have now issued a statement, while the NFL says its investigation remains open. MarShawn Lloyd has averaged 2.8 yards per carry, while Kaleb Johnson has averaged 3.9 yards per attempt. Jacobs recorded 1,329 rushing yards in his first season with Green Bay, followed by 929 yards the next year. Brown coming off IR ALCS Game 4 postponed Defense will win WNBA Finals 49ers vs. Commanders Preview: San Francisco Looks to Stay Undefeated Photo by: Darren Yamashita Stephan Stroud Fri, October 16, 2026 at 8:53 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads 49ers Aim to Keep Rolling on Monday Night The San Francisco 49ers return home Monday night looking to extend their undefeated start when they host the Washington Commanders at Levi's Stadium. San Francisco enters the Week 6 matchup at 5-0 after an exciting 32-29 road victory over the Seattle Seahawks, while Washington arrives at 1-3-1 following a frustrating 27-27 overtime tie against the New York Giants. The matchup presents two teams heading in different directions. The 49ers have found ways to win close games, while the Commanders are searching for consistency as they attempt to climb back into the NFC playoff conversation. Kickoff is scheduled for 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN and ABC. Brock Purdy Leads San Francisco's Offense Quarterback Brock Purdy has helped guide the 49ers through an impressive opening stretch. Although San Francisco has faced several challenging opponents, the offense has continued producing at important moments. Purdy threw two touchdown passes against Seattle and helped lead the game-winning drive that set up Eddy Piñeiro's decisive field goal. His ability to distribute the football and make smart decisions has been important to the team's success. Running back Christian McCaffrey remains another major weapon. His versatility as both a runner and receiver gives head coach Kyle Shanahan several ways to attack opposing defenses. San Francisco will look to establish its running game early, create favorable passing situations and control the tempo. The 49ers' offense has also benefited from contributions across the roster, allowing the team to remain productive even when individual drives become difficult. Jayden Daniels Looks to Spark Washington Washington will rely on quarterback Jayden Daniels to help generate offense against a San Francisco defense that has started the season strongly. Daniels demonstrated his playmaking ability against the Giants, rushing for 103 yards and two touchdowns while throwing for 199 yards. However, Washington's inability to finish the game left the team with a disappointing tie. Daniels' mobility could be one of the Commanders' biggest advantages. San Francisco will need disciplined defensive play to prevent him from escaping the pocket and creating explosive gains with his legs. Washington also needs better protection up front and more consistent execution on third downs. Sustaining drives will be particularly important against a 49ers team that has repeatedly capitalized on scoring opportunities. Kyle Shanahan vs. Dan Quinn The coaching matchup adds another layer to Monday night's game. Shanahan has San Francisco playing confident football, while Quinn needs Washington to respond after letting a potential victory slip away. For the Commanders, limiting turnovers and improving their second-half execution will be essential. The 49ers, meanwhile, will look to continue their balanced offensive approach and use their home-field advantage. A Major Test for Both Teams San Francisco has an opportunity to improve to 6-0 and strengthen its position in the NFC West. Washington needs a complete performance to show it can compete with one of the conference's unbeaten teams. With Purdy and McCaffrey leading the 49ers against Daniels and Washington's offense, Monday night's matchup offers an important test for both teams as the NFL season moves deeper into October.

NFL Betting Odds, Point Spread, Trends Really interesting quarterback matchup here. On one side, it's Washington's Jayden Daniels, a former NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year, Heisman Trophy winner and No. 2 overall draft pick who is as much of a dual-threat passer as there is. On the other, it's former Mr. Irrelevant draft choice Brock Purdy for San Francisco, and he might win his first NFL MVP Award this season. Purdy can run a little but is a pocket passer. Unbeaten San Francisco already leads the NFC West by two games and all due respect to fellow 5-0 team Minnesota, the 49ers look like the conference's best team so far. They are -205 favourites to win the NFC West , +300 leaders for the NFC title and +105 favourites for the No. 1 seed. Kyle Shanahan is right near the top at +650 for NFL Coach of the Year. 2026/27 NFL - Futures NFC Conference - Outright winner Washington had a terrific 2024 season when Daniels entered the league, but the team has regressed since then in part because Daniels has had trouble staying healthy – he's currently playing with a big brace on his non-throwing elbow. The Commanders (1-3-1) are last in the NFC East and you are starting to hear not-good rumblings about head coach Dan Quinn's future there. San Francisco has won the past two in the series, but they haven't played since 2023. NFL Player Odds and Props Back San Francisco quarterback Brock Purdy for at least two touchdown passes as he has 13 on the year and at least two in every game. Also like Washington's Jayden Daniels to not throw an interception as he hasn't in 76 attempts yet this year. If the Commanders' season continues to spiral, perhaps circle Week 5 for when ownership started thinking about making some majors changes on the coaching staff. Just an inexcusable 27-27 home tie against the Giants on Sunday. Washington blew a 14-point fourth-quarter lead but was in fairly easy field goal range near the end of overtime … before letting the clock run out with the kicking team not even on the field. Massive, massive blunder that's probably on QB Jayden Daniels for snapping the ball on the play previous, but he was told to try and gain more yards. So that's on embattled head coach Dan Quinn. Even Commanders minority owner Magic Johnson called out the team on social media. It marked Washington's first time failing to win when leading by at least 14 points in the fourth quarter at home since 1999. The franchise is now incredibly winless in six straight OT games (four losses, two ties). Daniels rushed for 103 yards and two scores in nine carries, only the second Washington QB with at least 100 yards on the ground since 1950. The 49ers were so impressive Sunday in a 32-29 win at defending Super Bowl champion Seattle to take control of the NFC West. The Niners had totaled only nine points in their previous two games against that stellar Seahawks defence. Brock Purdy threw two TDs and led two late scoring drives for the upset. Mike Evans blew up with seven catches for 113 yards and a TD. Purdy averaged 11.5 yards per attempt when targeting the future Hall of Famer Evans and 4.5 yards per attempt when targeting all others. Evans already has 21 first-down catches this year, among league leaders. San Francisco is 3-0 against last season's conference championship teams (Denver, Seattle and LA Rams) while the rest of the league is 5-11. The Niners have joined the 1999 Rams as the only teams in league history with three wins in their first five games of a season against clubs that had a minimum of 12 wins the prior year. away.blurb: Add ClutchPoints on Google Stefon Diggs has a legitimate chance to return for the Washington Commanders against the San Francisco 49ers on Monday Night Football, but his availability is not guaranteed. Washington listed Diggs as questionable after limited practices Friday and Saturday, leaving fantasy managers and the Commanders awaiting a final decision. Diggs missed Washington’s 27-27 tie against the New York Giants because of a hamstring injury. He opened Week 6 preparation by sitting out Thursday, then made enough progress to participate in the team’s final two practices. That is encouraging, especially after he failed to practice during the week preceding his Week 5 absence. Practicing on consecutive days gives Diggs a realistic path to playing, but Washington could still exercise caution. Hamstring injuries present a significant reinjury risk, and the Commanders have their bye immediately following Monday’s game. Holding Diggs out would provide him with two additional weeks of recovery before Washington returns in Week 8. Coach Dan Quinn did not confirm Saturday that Diggs would play. Instead, Washington gave him a questionable designation and will evaluate his condition leading up to kickoff. That uncertainty makes Monday’s inactive list essential, with official confirmation expected approximately 90 minutes before the game. The potential return would reunite Diggs, Terry McLaurin and Jayden Daniels for the first time since Week 2. away.blurb: Commanders Prepare for Return of NFL's ‘Next Great' Cornerback The Washington Commanders think they might have a special player in second-year cornerback Trey Amos. The problem is, Amos hasn't been available for quite some time. The Commanders are 1-3-1 and coming off an embarrassing 27-27 tie against the New York Giants , in which Washington let time run out instead of attempting a 41-yard field goal. "SECONDARY REINFORCEMENTS ARE HERE!" DC News Now's Alex Flume wrote on his official X account. " Nick Cross and Trey Amos were out getting involved at Commanders practice Wednesday. Dan Quinn said before practice that they are both expected to practice in full this week. Could be a massive boost for the Commanders pass defense this week." By all accounts, Amos has focused entirely on rehabbing his injury to return to the lineup — something that's taken considerably longer than anyone anticipated. "Dan Quinn said CB Trey Amos tweaked his ankle while in coverage on a deep ball to Terry McLaurin the other day," The Athletic's Nicki Jhabvala wrote on her official X account on August 10. "Quinn said he'll know more in a day or so about his timetable to return." Unlock the latest Heavy on Commanders news — direct to your inbox. Updated Oct 16, 2026 at 11:27pm Amos has missed 12 consecutive regular-season games since Week 10 of his rookie season, when he fractured his fibula against the Detroit Lions . Now, when the Commanders may need him most, Amos looks like he'll be back and will make his comeback in a Week 6 primetime showdown against the unbeaten San Francisco 49ers on Monday Night Football. Play Trey Amos: Total Focus on Returning to Commanders "Trey Amos has no hobbies," Commanders reporter Ben Standig wrote on his official X account. "No distractions. Just football. After 11 months and two injuries, the Commanders CB wants his life back." Amos was coming into his own when he got injured — he made 8 starts in 10 games as a rookie. The Commanders have had one glaring weakness on their defense this season and it's been with 3r-dyear cornerback Mike Sainristil . Getting Amos back and healthy could put Amos, Amik Robertson , and Rasul Douglas at two outside cornerback spots and one slot cornerback spot. That would be the best-case scenario — mainly because it keeps Sainristil off the field. "My big question for MNF, assuming Trey Amos can play: is Amik going back to nickel? Or is he playing outside until it's nickel package and then sliding inside? Amik's been stellar outside, but Trey and Rasul are two of your three best corners, and neither are playing inside," The Full Command Show wrote on its official X account. away.headline: Commanders hit with brutal injury news right before 49ers game
away.blurb: Washington opened with a narrow loss to the Philadelphia Eagles before following it with a 37-20 blowout loss to the Dallas Cowboys. They briefly turned things around by edging out the Seattle Seahawks 33-31, but then fell 30-13 to the Indianapolis Colts in Week 4. Even their 27-27 overtime tie with the New York Giants last weekend felt like a loss with how the game ended. The team desperately needs to regain momentum against San Francisco on Monday night. Unfortunately, they’ll need to do it without one of their best offensive players. According to NFL insider Jeremy Fowler, the Commanders plan to rule out running back Jacory-Croskey-Merritt for the 49ers game due to a groin injury. There’s no confirmed return date yet, but groin injuries have a tendency to linger if not properly managed, so this will be a situation to monitor after the 49ers game. Luckily, Washington will have a bye in Week 7, giving Croskey-Merritt two weeks to recover before the Commanders’ next game, a divisional showdown against the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday night. More news : Ravens Told to Hold Lamar Jackson Out as Injury Concerns Continue With Croskey-Merritt out for the 49ers game, carries would go to Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler. Unfortunately, both of those players are listed as questionable with injuries of their own: White with a shoulder injury and Ekeler with a chest injury. Both practiced in limited capacity on Friday. The Washington Commanders have stumbled through the first five weeks of the NFL season, heading into their Week 6 matchup against the San Francisco 49ers at 1-3-1. More news : Eagles Turn to Former Cowboys QB After Jalen Hurts Injury Croskey-Merritt first suffered a groin injury in preseason, but reinjured it during Washington’s tie with the Giants last weekend. He finished with 82 rushing yards and one touchdown on just 11 carries, averaging 7.5 yards per carry and putting together his best game of the season. But he didn’t practice on Thursday or Friday with the injury, which immediately put his availability for Monday’s game in doubt. More news : Raiders Consider Major Decision on Ashton Jeanty Amid Injury Concerns Jeremy McNichols is the only Commanders running back to have practiced in full on Friday while recovering from a quad injury on injured reserve. Washington would still need to activate him ahead of Monday night, but given all of the injuries to the other running backs, there’s a good chance that will happen. By Michael Gallagher Sports Content Coordinator 0 Share Newsweek is a Trust Project member See more of our trusted coverage when you search. Prefer Newsweek on Google to see more of our trusted coverage when you search. The San Francisco 49ers have had arguably the worst injury luck of any team in the NFL this season. More than 15 players are currently on the reserve/injured list while a handful of others are expected to miss some time with their respective ailments. San Francisco’s defense has been hit particularly hard, and star edge-rusher Nick Bosa’s absence over the last few weeks has been noticeable. Keion White has done his part to pick up the slack, but the rest of San Francisco’s pass-rush has left much to be desired, which is why Kristopher Knox of Bleacher Report believes the 49ers should make an all-in move to upgrade the position. Knox recently suggested the 49ers execute a trade with the winless Los Angeles Chargers for Pro Bowler Khalil Mack. “Los Angeles fell to 0-5 on Sunday, while Mack continues to be a legitimate difference-maker,” Knox wrote . “… Mack is playing on a one-year deal and should be interested in playing for a team that could get him his first career playoff win. “.. Mack should be the top target for any team with Super Bowl aspirations that happens to need help rushing opposing passers. It'll be a fairly significant surprise if he remains in Los Angeles beyond next month's deadline.” Despite multiple reports indicating the Chargers would want a fifth-round pick in exchange for Mack, Knox suggested it could take at least a conditional 2027 fourth-round pick to get a deal finalized given the demand for strong pass-rushers from contending teams. Through five games this season, Mack has logged 14 pressures, eight hurries, five tackles for loss, three QB hits, and three sacks with a pass-rush win-rate of 9.5%, according to Pro Football Focus. Adding that kind of production opposite White would be a big boost for the 49ers in the interim, and once Bosa comes back, it would make SF’s pass-rush all the more dangerous come playoff time.

home.headline: 49ers Owner On Verge of Returning From Lengthy NFL Suspension
home.blurb: The NFL came down hard on York on October 2, handing out a punishment following his arrest for soliciting a prostitute in Ohio that left a lasting stain on his legacy and his family’s legacy as owners of 1 of the NFL’s premier franchises. “49ers principal owner Jed York has been suspended for six regular-season games and fined $500,000 for violating the NFL’s Personal Conduct Policy, the NFL announced today,” The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero wrote. “During the time the league’s investigation has been proceeding, York has stayed away from the 49ers first three regular-season games, as well as from NFL league meetings. Those three missed games are counted toward his suspension, and he may return on Tuesday, Oct. 20.” 49ers Owner On Verge of Returning From Lengthy NFL Suspension Unlock the latest Heavy on 49ers news — direct to your inbox. San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York knew enough about how the NFL works to stay away from his team for the first 3 weeks of the season. Those weeks would eventually count toward a 6-game suspension that ends after his unbeaten team faces the Washington Commanders on Monday Night Football in Week 6. How York is received when he returns — if he begins to come around the team again — is another issue entirely after his arrest for soliciting prostitution in Ohio this summer. NFL Came Down Hard on 49ers Owner Jed York “Just in: San Francisco 49ers principal owner Jed York has been suspended for six regular-season games and fined $500,000 for violating the NFL’s Personal Conduct Policy,” ESPN’s Adam Schefter wrote on his official X account following the suspension. York was arrested on August 23 at the Wheat Hill Mobile Home Community in East Palestine, Ohio, as part of an online prostitution sting conducted by local authorities. “Today, the NFL concluded its review, and I accept its decision in full,” York said in a prepared statement . “To my family, to the players, coaches, and employees of the San Francisco 49ers, to our fans and partners, I am deeply sorry. This was an inexcusable mistake and I take full responsibility. What I did does not reflect my values or the man I strive to be for my family. While I fell short of the model I want to set for my sons, I now hope to show them the importance of owning up to one’s failures, and that even our worst moments teach us to be better. Leading the 49ers is a privilege, and one I don’t take lightly. Your trust will have to be earned back over time, and I look forward to that work ahead.” Jed York Stayed Away From 49ers After Arrest York stayed away from the 49ers since his arrest and while the NFL conducted its investigation — the 49ers are now 5-0 and one of just three remaining unbeaten teams.
